chapters.title: Staying Together
chapters.summary: In this chapter: playing together; singing together; laughing together; types of families.

lessons.title: Playing Together

activities.prompt: What do Bela and her family enjoy doing together?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Playing Together
activities.body: Bela has two brothers, Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu. They enjoy playing chhupan-chhupai outside together. At home, everyone loves playing peek-a-boo with Bishu. Someone hides and suddenly appears again. The family has a garden with flowering plants. Relatives, friends and neighbours visit the garden. They sit, talk, share jokes and laugh together. Bela’s father and mother get tired after a hard day’s work. Everyone enjoys spending the evenings together.
keyPoints: Banku Bhaiya and Bishu are Bela’s two brothers.
They enjoy playing chhupan-chhupai outside.
At home, everyone plays peek-a-boo with Bishu.
Visitors sit, talk, share jokes and laugh in the garden.
activities.explanation: This card introduces the family’s games, garden visits and evening togetherness.

activities.prompt: After a hard day's work, Bela's parents are tired. How can the evening still be fun for everyone?
steps: The garden's flowering plants give everyone one shared place to meet.
Relatives, friends and neighbours visit it, so the garden brings people together.
Visitors sit, talk, share jokes and laugh, so visits become shared fun.
Everyone enjoys evenings together, so tired parents can join the happy time.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which game do Bela and her brothers enjoy playing outside?
options: chhupan-chhupai
peek-a-boo
garden visits
evening talks
activities.explanation: They all enjoy playing this game outside together.

activities.prompt: Bela has two sisters.
activities.explanation: Bela has two brothers, Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu.

activities.prompt: Match each place with the activity that happens there.
activities.explanation: Each activity matches the place described in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Bela and her brothers enjoy playing ______ outside together.
activities.hint: This game is played outside with Banku Bhaiya and Bishu.
activities.explanation: The lesson says they enjoy this game outside together.

activities.prompt: What do the garden visitors do together?
options: They hide and stay hidden.
They plant more flowers.
They sit, talk and laugh.
They work and then rest.
activities.explanation: Visitors sit, talk, share jokes and laugh together.

activities.prompt: Put these events in the order described in the lesson.
items: Bela’s father and mother finish a hard day’s work
Bela’s father and mother get tired
Everyone enjoys spending the evenings together
activities.explanation: Work comes first, tiredness follows, and everyone enjoys the evening together.

activities.prompt: Bela's parents rest after a hard day's work. What may happen in the evening?
options: They may sit, talk, share jokes, and laugh together.
They may sit in silence and avoid every visitor.
They may leave the garden before anyone joins them.
They may work again instead of spending time together.

why.They may sit in silence and avoid every: This mistakes shared fun for silence and avoidance.
why.They may leave the garden before anyone: This mistakes the welcoming garden for a place people leave.
why.They may work again instead of spending: This mistakes evening rest for more work instead of shared time.

activities.explanation: says visitors sit, talk, share jokes, and laugh together.

activities.prompt: Bela and her brothers enjoy chhupan-chhupai outside. Which way fairly checks this?
options: Ask Bela, Banku Bhaiya, and little Bishu.
Ask only Banku Bhaiya about both brothers.
Ask the neighbours about the brothers' games.
Ask the garden visitors about the family at home.

why.Ask only Banku Bhaiya about both brother: Asking only one player can miss what the others enjoy.
why.Ask the neighbours about the brothers' g: The neighbours visit the garden, but their answers may miss the players' choices.
why.Ask the garden visitors about the family: The visitors speak about visits, not about what the family enjoys.

activities.explanation: This asks each player, so every player can give an answer.

activities.prompt: In peek-a-boo, Bela hides while little Bishu covers his eyes. What happens next?
options: Bela suddenly appears again before Bishu looks.
Bela stays hidden until everyone leaves the house.
Bela leaves home and plays outside alone.
Bela begins another game with the visitors.

why.Bela stays hidden until everyone leaves: This mistakes appearing again for staying hidden.
why.Bela leaves home and plays outside alone: This mistakes the game for leaving and playing alone.
why.Bela begins another game with the visito: This mistakes the next move for starting with garden visitors.

activities.explanation: says the hidden person suddenly appears again.

activities.prompt: Bela and her brothers want to play chhupan-chhupai. Where and why should they play?
options: They should play outside their house because they enjoy it together.
They should play inside their house because the game stays there.
They should play with visitors because visitors join every game.
They should play alone because their brothers dislike games.

why.They should play inside their house beca: This mistakes chhupan-chhupai for a game that must stay inside.
why.They should play with visitors because v: This mistakes their usual players for the garden visitors.
why.They should play alone because their bro: This mistakes enjoying games together for preferring to play alone.

activities.explanation: Facts 1.2 and 1.5 say they enjoy playing together outside their house.

lessons.title: Singing Together

activities.prompt: Which songs might Dadiji teach us on a rainy day?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Rainy Day Together
activities.body: On rainy days, the family sits together under a small shelter in the garden. The grandparents join them, and Bela thinks this is great fun. They play antakshari and snakes and ladders. Dadiji makes hot pakodas and tea. She also sings songs about the rain and teaches the others a few. The song shows dark clouds, coming rain, paper boats, birds and dancing peacocks.
keyPoints: The family and grandparents enjoy rainy days together.
Dadiji makes pakodas and tea and sings songs.
The rain song includes clouds, rain, paper boats, birds and peacocks.
activities.explanation: The rain brings the family together for food, games and singing.

activities.prompt: During Singing Together, it is raining. The family sits under the small garden shelter, and Dadiji sings a rain song. What can the others do?
steps: Dadiji has taught the others a few of her songs.
This means the others can join her in singing.
The family sits together under the garden shelter on rainy days.
So the family can sing Dadiji's rain song together while it rains.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Who Makes the Rainy-Day Treats?
activities.prompt: Who makes hot pakodas and tea during the rains?
options: Bela
Dadiji
The grandparents
The others
activities.explanation: Great choice! Dadiji makes hot pakodas and tea during the rains.

activities.title: Dadiji’s Song
activities.prompt: Dadiji often sings songs about the ______.
activities.hint: Think about the weather during the family’s special outdoor days.
activities.explanation: Well done! Dadiji often sings songs about the rain.

activities.title: Floating in Puddles
activities.prompt: Which does the rain song say floats in puddles?
options: Dark clouds
Birds
Peacocks
Paper boats
activities.explanation: Yes! The song mentions paper boats floating in puddles.

activities.title: Rain Song Pictures
activities.prompt: Match each song detail with its picture.
activities.explanation: Excellent matching! Every pair comes from the rain song.

activities.title: Only Rain Song Details
activities.prompt: Which set contains only details from the rain song?
options: Paper boats, birds, peacocks
Dark clouds, hot tea, birds
Rain, pakodas, peacocks
Snakes and ladders, clouds, birds
activities.explanation: You found them! Paper boats, birds and peacocks all appear in the song.

activities.prompt: It is raining, and the family sits under the small garden shelter. What might Dadiji make?
options: Hot pakodas and tea for everyone under the shelter.
Hot pakodas and tea for everyone outside the shelter.
Paper boats and tea for everyone under the shelter.
Dark clouds and tea for everyone under the shelter.

why.Hot pakodas and tea for everyone outside: The family is under the shelter, not outside it.
why.Paper boats and tea for everyone under t: Paper boats are in the song, not Dadiji's rainy-day food.
why.Dark clouds and tea for everyone under t: Dark clouds are described in the song, not served as tea.

activities.explanation: Dadiji makes hot pakodas and tea during the rains.

activities.prompt: Everyone, including the grandparents, eats Dadiji's pakodas. Which plan best checks if the whole family enjoys them?
options: Ask each family member after everyone eats together.
Ask only Bela before anyone eats the pakodas.
Ask Dadiji alone what everyone else likes.
Ask the grandparents but leave out Bela.

why.Ask only Bela before anyone eats the pak: It checks only Bela and asks before she eats.
why.Ask Dadiji alone what everyone else like: Dadiji cannot tell what every other member enjoys.
It leaves out Bela, so it does not check everyone.

activities.explanation: It asks every family member and uses the shared meal.

activities.prompt: Someone says, “Dadiji sings alone because nobody else knows her songs.” Why is this claim weak?
options: Dadiji has taught others a few of her songs.
Dadiji sings alone because rain songs have no words.
Dadiji sings alone because only Bela can hear her.
Dadiji sings alone because games stop her singing.

why.Dadiji sings alone because rain songs ha: The rain song's words include clouds, rain, and boats.
why.Dadiji sings alone because only Bela can: The fact does not say that only Bela can hear Dadiji.
why.Dadiji sings alone because games stop he: The facts say games and songs both happen during rainy days.

activities.explanation: Teaching others songs makes the claim about nobody else false.

lessons.title: Laughing Together

activities.prompt: How does everyone join in the games with laughter?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Games and a Four-Legged Friend
activities.body: Dadaji has taught Banku and Bela some games. He used to play those games with his friends when he was their age. Now Dadaji joins the children in some of their games. Their dog Shiru runs around with them, barks and wags his tail with joy. Shiru has a special place in Bela's home and is treated as a member of the family. The children's friends also love playing with Shiru.
keyPoints: Dadaji teaches and joins in the games.
Shiru plays, barks and wags his tail with joy.
Shiru is treated as a member of the family.
activities.explanation: This lesson is about games, laughter and a happy dog named Shiru.

activities.prompt: Dadaji plays with Banku and Bela while Shiru runs around. Why is this more than a game?
steps: Dadaji once played these games with friends, so he brings shared memories.
He joins the children, while Shiru barks happily, so play includes him.
They never hurt Shiru and share food, showing family care.
Playing and caring together show the heart of Laughing Together.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Who has taught Banku and Bela some games?
options: Dadaji
Shiru
A neighbour
A shopkeeper
activities.explanation: Dadaji has taught Banku and Bela some games. Well spotted!

activities.prompt: Banku and Bela share their food with ______.
activities.hint: The dog who plays with the children.
activities.explanation: Good try! Banku and Bela share their food with Shiru.

activities.prompt: Shiru barks and wags his tail with joy.
activities.explanation: Yes, Shiru is a happy dog who barks and wags his tail.

activities.prompt: Why is Shiru treated as a member of the family?
options: He has a place in Bela's home
He sleeps outside in the garden
He runs away from the children
He only comes to eat food
activities.explanation: Yes! Shiru has a special place in Bela's home, so he is treated as family.

activities.prompt: Match each one to what it does.
pairs: Taught Banku and Bela some games
activities.explanation: Great matching! Everyone in this lesson plays and shares together.

activities.prompt: Which set of things about Shiru is true?
options: He has a special place and gets food
He has no special place and gets food
He has a special place but gets no food
He has no place and gets no food
activities.explanation: Correct! Shiru has a special place in Bela's home, and they share food with him.

activities.prompt: Banku and Bela play games Dadaji once played with friends. Why does this show "Laughing Together"?
options: Playing and caring bring everyone together in shared fun.
Only the person teaching games can join the fun.
Shiru’s barking shows why games should end early.
Playing games matters more than caring for each other.

why.Only the person teaching games can join: This wrongly makes the teacher separate from the fun.
why.Shiru’s barking shows why games should e: This wrongly treats happy barking as a problem.
why.Playing games matters more than caring f: This wrongly puts games above the family care shown.

activities.explanation: Dadaji shares games, and the children care for Shiru.

activities.prompt: Banku and Bela choose one of Dadaji’s games. What will Dadaji most likely do next?
options: Join the children for some of their play.
Watch the children play but never join them.
Ask Shiru to play the game by himself.
Leave the game to find friends from long ago.

why.Watch the children play but never join t: This mistakes watching for joining the children’s play.
This wrongly makes Shiru the only one who can play.
why.Leave the game to find friends from long: This wrongly assumes his old friends replace the children.

activities.explanation: He joins some of the children’s games, so joining fits.

activities.prompt: Shiru barks while playing near the children. Why is calling him only a guest wrong?
options: He has a special place and is treated as family.
Barking shows that visitors should stay outside.
Running around shows that he is not inside.
A guest should never have a special home place.

why.Barking shows that visitors should stay: This wrongly treats barking as proof of being outside.
why.Running around shows that he is not insi: This wrongly treats running around as staying outside.
why.A guest should never have a special home: This wrongly says guests cannot have special places.

activities.explanation: His special place and family treatment show he belongs.

activities.prompt: The children’s friends come to play near Shiru. What will the friends most likely do?
options: Join in playing with Shiru too.
Stay away because Shiru barks.
Ask the children to send Shiru away.
Watch the game while ignoring Shiru.

This wrongly treats barking as a reason to stay away.
This wrongly assumes friends dislike Shiru’s presence.
This wrongly separates friends’ play from Shiru.

activities.explanation: The children’s friends love playing with Shiru, so joining fits.

activities.prompt: Shiru is treated as a member of Bela’s family. Which action is the fairest test of Banku and Bela’s care?
options: Watch if they share food and never hurt him.
Watch if Shiru barks and wags his tail.
Watch if Dadaji joins some of the children’s games.
Watch if their friends also love playing with Shiru.

Shiru’s happy actions show his mood, not their care.
why.Watch if Dadaji joins some of the childr: Dadaji joining play shows his place, not their care.
why.Watch if their friends also love playing: Friends playing with Shiru show their welcome, not their care.

activities.explanation: This is fair because sharing and avoiding harm show care.

lessons.title: Types of Families

activities.prompt: What makes a family a family?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Families can be different
activities.body: Families can be big, small or different from one another. Every family is valued and loved. A family is a group of people who care for one another. It may include parents, children, grandparents and other elders. Some families have few members, while others have many. Families also love and care for animals, trees and plants. There are many types of families in a neighbourhood.
keyPoints: Families can be big, small or different.
People in families care for one another.
Families also care for animals, trees and plants.
activities.explanation: Every family is valued and loved.

activities.prompt: Can a parent, child, grandparent and parrot belong to one family?
steps: A family can include parents and children, because families can be different.
A parrot can also belong, because families love and care for animals.
So they can all belong, because families care for people and animals.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Every family is valued and loved.
activities.explanation: Every family is valued and loved.

activities.prompt: Which animals can also be part of a family?
options: Parrots, cats and trees
Parrots, trees and plants
Parrots, cats and goats
Cats, grandparents and plants
activities.explanation: Parrots, cats and goats can also be part of a family.

activities.prompt: Every family has the same number of members.
activities.explanation: Families may have only a few members or many members.

activities.prompt: A family may have only a few members or ______ members.
activities.hint: Some families have more members than others.
activities.explanation: A family may have only a few members or many members.

activities.prompt: A family cares for a parrot, a tree and plants. What does this show?
options: They only love parents and children
They never care for any trees
They always need more members
They love and care for them
activities.explanation: Families also love and care for animals, trees and plants.

activities.prompt: Two neighbours care for each other. What should you conclude?
options: They form a family, because they care for one another.
They form a family, because they live near each other.
They form a family, because they know each other well.
They form a family, because they have the same size.

why.They form a family, because they live ne: This mistake thinks living near someone makes a family.
why.They form a family, because they know ea: This mistake thinks knowing someone well makes a family.
why.They form a family, because they have th: This mistake thinks having the same size makes a family.

activities.explanation: This is right because families are groups who care for one another.

activities.prompt: A family feeds and waters its parrot. What can you say?
options: The parrot can be part of that family.
The parrot must live far from that family.
The parrot cannot belong to that family.
Only people can belong to that family.

why.The parrot must live far from that famil: This mistake thinks animals cannot stay with their family.
This mistake thinks animals cannot be family members.
This mistake thinks families include only people.

activities.explanation: This is right because animals can be part of a family.

activities.prompt: A grandparent helps care for a child. What does this show?
options: The grandparent can belong to the child's family.
The grandparent must belong to a different family.
The grandparent cannot belong to the child's family.
Only parents can care for that child.

why.The grandparent must belong to a differe: This mistake thinks only parents and children make a family.
why.The grandparent cannot belong to the chi: This mistake thinks grandparents cannot belong to a family.
This mistake thinks only parents care for family members.

activities.explanation: This is right because a family can include grandparents.

activities.prompt: Two groups are compared. Which check finds a family fairly?
options: Check whether they care for one another.
Check whether they have the same address.
Check whether they have the same age.
Check whether they have the same pets.

why.Check whether they have the same address: This mistake thinks sharing an address defines a family.
This mistake thinks having the same age defines a family.
This mistake thinks sharing pets defines a family.

activities.explanation: This is right because caring for one another defines a family.

activities.prompt: A neighbourhood has small and big families. How should we treat both?
options: Both are valued and loved, because every family is.
Only the bigger family is valued and loved.
Only the smaller family should receive care.
The family with more members should lead.

why.Only the bigger family is valued and lov: This mistake thinks bigger families deserve more love.
why.Only the smaller family should receive c: This mistake thinks smaller families need less care.
why.The family with more members should lead: This mistake thinks more members make a family better.

activities.explanation: This is right because every family is valued and loved.

lessons.title: Helping Each Other

activities.prompt: How do people in a family help each other every day?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Working Together
activities.body: Bela's family helps each other with housework. They cook, clean and shop for groceries. Dadiji oils and braids Bela's hair in the morning. She hums a song while braiding it. Dadaji loves gardening, which means working in the garden. Bela helps there. Banku helps with cleaning and chopping vegetables. Banku and Bela help parents and grandparents. Munni and Kusum Mausi are close friends. Children learn from family and neighbours.
keyPoints: Family members share housework and daily jobs.
Banku and Bela help their parents and grandparents.
Family friends and neighbours can help children learn.
activities.explanation: Helping each other makes family life happier and more shared.

activities.prompt: Bela’s parents have cooking, cleaning and shopping to share. How can helping each other help at home?
steps: Housework includes cooking, cleaning and shopping for groceries.
Sharing is useful because the parents can help while jobs are done.
Banku and Bela also join in with some daily work.
So helping each other means sharing useful jobs at home.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Who Hums a Song?
activities.prompt: Who hums a song while she braids Bela's hair?
options: Dadiji
Dadaji
Banku
Bela
activities.explanation: Dadiji hums a song while she braids Bela's hair.

activities.title: Banku's Helping
activities.prompt: Banku helps only with chopping vegetables.
activities.explanation: Banku helps with cleaning and chopping vegetables.

activities.title: Dadaji's Favourite Work
activities.prompt: Dadaji loves ______.
activities.hint: This work happens in the garden.
activities.explanation: Dadaji loves gardening, so this word completes the sentence.

activities.title: Match the Helpers
activities.prompt: Match each person with the task or interest.
activities.explanation: Dadiji braids hair, Dadaji loves gardening, Banku chops vegetables, and Bela helps in the garden.

activities.title: Colours from Flowers
activities.prompt: Munni uses colours made from different dried flowers.
activities.explanation: Yes. Munni uses colours made from different dried flowers.

activities.title: Order of Topics
activities.prompt: Put these topics in the order they appear in your book.
items: Munni is a close family friend
Children learn from family and neighbours
activities.explanation: These topics appear on pages 10, 11 and 12, in that order.

activities.prompt: Bela’s parents help each other with the housework. Their housework includes cooking, cleaning and shopping for groceries. Why can sharing help the parents?
options: They can each do some jobs and help the other.
They can leave all housework to Banku and Bela.
They can do all jobs without helping anyone.
They can keep every job only for themselves.

why.They can leave all housework to Banku an: Banku and Bela help with some work, not all housework.
why.They can do all jobs without helping any: Doing all jobs alone is the opposite of helping.
why.They can keep every job only for themsel: Keeping every job alone misses the parents’ shared work.

activities.explanation: One parent can help while the other does a job.

activities.prompt: Cooking is part of the family housework. Banku helps with cleaning and chopping vegetables. Bela helps Dadaji in the garden. Dadiji hums while braiding Bela’s hair. Munni uses colours made from dried flowers. What can Banku do to help with cooking?
options: Chop vegetables to help with the cooking.
Help Dadaji with garden work instead.
Make colours from different dried flowers.
Hum a song while doing the cooking.

This mixes up Bela’s garden help with Banku’s.
why.Make colours from different dried flower: The flower-colour task belongs to Munni, not Banku.
Humming belongs to Dadiji’s hair braiding, not cooking.

activities.explanation: Chopping vegetables is one of Banku’s helping tasks.

activities.prompt: Dadaji loves gardening. Bela helps Dadaji in the garden. Banku and Bela help their parents and grandparents with some daily work. What does Bela’s garden help show?
options: She is helping her family with daily work.
She is helping her family avoid all work.
She is doing work that nobody else enjoys.
She is learning daily work only from neighbours.

why.She is helping her family avoid all work: Helping in the garden is work, not avoiding work.
why.She is doing work that nobody else enjoy: Dadaji loves gardening, so someone does enjoy it.
why.She is learning daily work only from nei: Children learn from family members and neighbours, not only neighbours.

activities.explanation: Bela helps Dadaji and also helps family members.

activities.prompt: Bela’s parents help each other with the housework. Their housework includes cooking, cleaning and shopping for groceries. A child says, "They never do one job alone." What is the best reply?
options: They may do some jobs together instead of alone.
They must leave all housework to Banku.
They only shop and never do other work.
They never help because they always work alone.

Banku helps with some work, but the parents still help each other.
The parents’ housework includes cooking and cleaning too.
why.They never help because they always work: This claim contradicts the parents helping each other.

activities.explanation: Helping each other can mean doing housework jobs together.

lessons.title: Fun with Family and Friends

activities.prompt: What fun surprises can a family holiday bring?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Happy Day in the Park
activities.body: Everyone went to the park with Dadaji on a holiday. Many friends were playing pitthoo there. The players called out to one another as they ran fast and placed stones quickly. Bela and her friends joined the game and made two teams. Rohit, Niku and Ronnie tried to hit the other team. After about twenty minutes, Dadaji bought everyone icecream. It became dark, so they went home.
keyPoints: Everyone went to the park with Dadaji on a holiday.
Bela and her friends made two teams for pitthoo.
Dadaji bought everyone icecream before it became dark.
activities.explanation: Here is the whole story of the park day.

activities.prompt: How did the pitthoo game become a happy time for everyone?
steps: Bela and her friends made two teams, because they could play against each other.
Dadaji scattered the stones, because players could then run and pile them up.
Rohit, Niku and Ronnie tried to hit the other team, because both teams were playing.
They played, laughed and ate icecream together, so the day became lots of fun.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Who went to the park with everyone?
options: Dadaji
Rohit
Niku
Bela
activities.explanation: Dadaji took everyone to the park on a holiday.

activities.prompt: Many friends were playing ______ at the park.
activities.hint: It is the game with stones in the park.
activities.explanation: Lots of friends were playing pitthoo together.

activities.prompt: What did Dadaji bring to the park?
options: a bat
a ball
a kite
a book
activities.explanation: Dadaji brought a ball and scattered the stones with it.

activities.prompt: Match each action to the right person or group.
pairs: Tried to hit the other team
activities.explanation: Everyone had a part in the game at the park.

activities.prompt: Put the events of the day in order.
items: Everyone went to the park with Dadaji
Dadaji scattered the stones with the ball
It became dark, so they went home
activities.explanation: The day went from playing to icecream and then home.

activities.prompt: Why did they go home from the park?
options: It started to rain
The game was over
It became dark
The park closed early
activities.explanation: It became dark, so everyone went home.

activities.prompt: At the park, Dadaji scatters stones with a ball during pitthoo. What will the players most likely do next?
options: They will run quickly and pile up the stones.
They will buy icecream and wait for dark.
They will leave the stones and play quietly.
They will make one new team and rest.

why.They will buy icecream and wait for dark: Icecream came later, after about twenty minutes of playing.
why.They will leave the stones and play quie: Leaving the stones would stop the pile-up part of pitthoo.
Making one new team would remove the other team.

activities.explanation: They ran quickly to pile up the stones after Dadaji scattered them.

activities.prompt: Bela and her friends make two teams during pitthoo. Why do they make teams?
options: So players could try to hit the other team.
So everyone would play alone in the park.
So they could stop playing the game.
So Dadaji could then buy everyone icecream.

why.So everyone would play alone in the park: Playing alone removes the other team from the game.
Making teams lets the players keep playing pitthoo.
why.So Dadaji could then buy everyone icecre: Buying icecream was a later treat, not the reason for teams.

activities.explanation: Rohit, Niku and Ronnie tried to hit the other team.

activities.prompt: Rohit says, "Rohit, Niku and Ronnie only watched the game." Why is this claim flawed?
options: They played and tried to hit the other team.
They only called out but never played together.
They played alone after the park game ended.
They bought icecream but never joined the game.

why.They only called out but never played to: Calling out alone does not show that they only watched.
why.They played alone after the park game en: The game had two teams, so they did not play alone.
why.They bought icecream but never joined th: Buying icecream came later, after about twenty minutes of play.

activities.explanation: They tried to hit the other team, so they were playing.

activities.prompt: Dadaji does not scatter the stones with the ball. Which part of the game is most likely missing?
options: Players running quickly to pile up stones.
Players making two teams for the game.
Players calling out to one another.
Players going home when it gets dark.

Two teams could still be made without Dadaji scattering stones.
Players could still call out even if the stones were not scattered.
The trip home depends on darkness, not on scattering stones.

activities.explanation: Without scattered stones, the running and pile-up part is missing.

activities.context: On an evening, Bela, Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu go to the open space outside their house to play chhupan-chhupai together. At home, everyone loves playing peek-a-boo with Bishu. Relatives, friends and neighbours also visit the family’s garden, which has several flowering plants. The visitors sit, talk, share jokes and laugh while Bela’s tired father and mother enjoy the evening with everyone.
activities.prompt: Banku Bhaiya is playing peek-a-boo with Bishu at home. What happens next?
options: He comes back into view after hiding.
He stays out of sight for the rest of the day.
He changes the game into chhupan-chhupai.
He leaves home and waits in the open space.

why.He stays out of sight for the rest of th: A player does not remain out of sight throughout the day.
why.He changes the game into chhupan-chhupai: Chhupan-chhupai is a different game from peek-a-boo.
why.He leaves home and waits in the open spa: The open space is used for chhupan-chhupai, not this at-home game.

activities.explanation: Peek-a-boo includes hiding and then coming back into view.

activities.context: On an evening, Bela, Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu go to the open space outside their house to play chhupan-chhupai together. At home, everyone loves playing peek-a-boo with Bishu. Relatives, friends and neighbours also visit the family’s garden, which has several flowering plants. The visitors sit, talk, share jokes and laugh while Bela’s tired father and mother enjoy the evening with everyone.
activities.prompt: Bela’s father and mother have finished a hard day’s work. What is most likely part of their evening?
options: They stay for the evening activities with everyone else.
They leave the garden as soon as the visitors arrive.
They ask Bela and her brothers to finish their games.
They spend the evening apart from everyone else.

why.They leave the garden as soon as the vis: The visitors have come to spend time in the garden.
why.They ask Bela and her brothers to finish: Bela and her brothers enjoy playing together.
why.They spend the evening apart from everyo: The family enjoys spending the evening together.

activities.explanation: Everyone enjoys spending the evenings together.

activities.prompt: How does peek-a-boo match the family’s love of playing together, and how is it different from chhupan-chhupai?
activities.answer: Peek-a-boo is a game the family enjoys at home. One player hides and then suddenly comes back into view. Chhupan-chhupai is played by Bela and her brothers in the open space outside their house. Thus, both bring family members together, but they happen in different places and involve different actions.
points: Peek-a-boo is played at home.
Someone hides and then comes back into view.
Chhupan-chhupai is played outside.
The games involve different actions and places.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: On a rainy day, Bela and her family sit under a small shelter in the garden. Bela thinks it is great fun to sit outside when it rains. They play antakshari and snakes and ladders together while Dadiji makes hot pakodas and tea. Everyone, including the grandparents, sits together and enjoys the pakodas. Dadiji often sings songs about the rain and has taught the others a few of her songs.
activities.prompt: It has just started raining. What should the family do next to join the rainy-day activity described in the case?
options: Go outside and gather beneath the garden's small covering.
Wait for the rain to stop before doing anything.
Go to the garden but sit apart under different trees.
Move outside without using any covering.

why.Wait for the rain to stop before doing a: Waiting would not follow the activity described.
why.Go to the garden but sit apart under dif: Sitting apart does not match the family sitting together.
The case describes using a shelter, not going uncovered.

activities.explanation: The family gathers under the garden shelter on rainy days.

activities.context: On a rainy day, Bela and her family sit under a small shelter in the garden. Bela thinks it is great fun to sit outside when it rains. They play antakshari and snakes and ladders together while Dadiji makes hot pakodas and tea. Everyone, including the grandparents, sits together and enjoys the pakodas. Dadiji often sings songs about the rain and has taught the others a few of her songs.
activities.prompt: Bela wants to act out one picture from Dadiji's rain song. Where should she float her paper boat?
options: In a puddle outside.
In Dadiji's hot tea.
On a branch where the birds sit.
Among the dark clouds in the sky.

Hot tea is not a puddle.
The birds sit on trees, but the boats float in puddles.
Clouds are in the sky and cannot hold a floating boat.

activities.explanation: The song describes paper boats floating in puddles.

activities.prompt: How does Dadiji make the rain songs a shared family activity, and how do the games fit into the rainy-day gathering?
activities.answer: Dadiji often sings songs about the rain and teaches a few to the others, so everyone can join in. The family also plays antakshari and snakes and ladders while sitting together under the small shelter. Together, the songs and games make the rainy gathering enjoyable for Bela and everyone else.
points: Dadiji sings songs about the rain.
She teaches some of her songs to the others.
The family plays antakshari and snakes and ladders.
Everyone gathers together under the shelter.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: At Bela’s home, Banku and Bela play a game Dadaji taught them. Dadaji joins them; he used to play those games with his friends when he was their age. Shiru runs around, barking and wagging his tail with joy. He has a special place there and is treated as a member of the family. The children’s friends love playing with Shiru, and Banku and Bela share their food with him while never hurting him.
activities.prompt: Banku and Bela’s friends are playing near Shiru. What are they most likely to do next?
options: Join in and play with him.
Stay away from him.
Ask Dadaji to stop the game.
Wait for him to leave before playing.

Nothing suggests that they dislike Shiru.
Dadaji joins the children’s games rather than stopping them.
Shiru plays happily with the children and their friends.

activities.explanation: The children’s friends love playing with Shiru.

activities.context: At Bela’s home, Banku and Bela play a game Dadaji taught them. Dadaji joins them; he used to play those games with his friends when he was their age. Shiru runs around, barking and wagging his tail with joy. He has a special place there and is treated as a member of the family. The children’s friends love playing with Shiru, and Banku and Bela share their food with him while never hurting him.
activities.prompt: Banku and Bela are eating, and Shiru is nearby. What best shows that he is treated as a member of the family?
options: Give him some of their food.
Keep every bit of food for themselves.
Give him food only after he stops barking.
Give their food to Dadaji instead.

Sharing food fits how they treat him as family.
why.Give him food only after he stops barkin: Shiru barks and wags his tail with joy, not because he must wait for food.
The children share their own food with Shiru, not give it to Dadaji.

activities.explanation: Banku and Bela share their food with Shiru.

activities.prompt: Explain how Dadaji’s games connect him with Banku and Bela.
activities.answer: Dadaji taught Banku and Bela some games. He used to play those games with his friends when he was their age. Now he joins Banku and Bela in some games. This means the games connect Dadaji’s earlier play with the children’s play today.
points: Dadaji taught the children games.
He played the games with his friends when he was their age.
He now joins Banku and Bela in some games.
The same games link his past and present play.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A family in a neighbourhood has parents, children and grandparents. When a grandparent needs support, relatives and neighbours love, care for and support the family. The family also includes a parrot, which is part of the family. The parents, children and grandparents all care for one another. The family is valued and loved, like other families in the neighbourhood.
activities.prompt: The parrot is also part of the family. Who should love and care for it?
options: Every person in the family
Only the parents
Only the neighbours
Only the grandparents

why.Only the parents: Caring for the parrot is not limited to the parents.
why.Only the neighbours: Neighbours love, care for and support family members.
why.Only the grandparents: Grandparents help care for the family, but they are not the only carers.

activities.explanation: Everyone in a family loves and cares for the other members.

activities.context: A family in a neighbourhood has parents, children and grandparents. When a grandparent needs support, relatives and neighbours love, care for and support the family. The family also includes a parrot, which is part of the family. The parents, children and grandparents all care for one another. The family is valued and loved, like other families in the neighbourhood.
activities.prompt: A grandparent needs support, and relatives and neighbours are nearby. What should they do?
options: Offer loving care and support to the person
Wait for the family to stop caring for the person
Ask the person to leave the family
Care only for their own relatives

why.Wait for the family to stop caring for t: Family members continue to care for one another.
why.Ask the person to leave the family: Asking someone to leave would not show care for a family member.
why.Care only for their own relatives: Their care is not limited only to relatives of the neighbours.

activities.explanation: Relatives and neighbours love, care for and support family members.

activities.context: A family in a neighbourhood has parents, children and grandparents. When a grandparent needs support, relatives and neighbours love, care for and support the family. The family also includes a parrot, which is part of the family. The parents, children and grandparents all care for one another. The family is valued and loved, like other families in the neighbourhood.
activities.prompt: A family has many members, while another family has only a few. What is the best way for a child to understand them?
options: Respect both groups because each one cares for its own members
Treat the larger group as the only genuine family
Treat the smaller group as less important
Expect both groups to have exactly the same members

why.Treat the larger group as the only genui: Every family is valued, regardless of how many members it has.
why.Treat the smaller group as less importan: Having fewer members does not make a family less valued.
why.Expect both groups to have exactly the s: Families can be different and do not need exactly the same members.

activities.explanation: A family may have few or many members, and every family is valued.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between a big family and a small family using what you know about families.
activities.answer: A big family may have many members, while a small family may have only a few. The number of members does not change the value of the family. People in the family care for one another, and relatives and neighbours can also love, care for and support the family.
points: A big family may have many members.
A small family may have only a few members.
Every family is valued and loved.
Family members and relatives and neighbours provide care and support.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: One morning, Dadiji oils Bela’s hair and braids it while humming a song. Banku cleans the house and chops vegetables to help his parents. Bela goes to the garden to help Dadaji, who loves gardening. Bela’s parents also help each other with cooking, cleaning, and shopping for groceries. Banku and Bela give daily help to their grandparents, and children in the family learn from relatives and neighbours.
activities.prompt: Dadiji begins to oil Bela’s hair. What should continue as part of the hair-care routine?
options: She will make a melody as she plaits Bela’s hair.
She will begin chopping vegetables for the family.
She will start helping Dadaji in the garden.
She will shop for the household’s groceries.

why.She will start helping Dadaji in the gar: Bela helps Dadaji in the garden.

activities.explanation: Dadiji hums while braiding Bela’s hair.

activities.context: One morning, Dadiji oils Bela’s hair and braids it while humming a song. Banku cleans the house and chops vegetables to help his parents. Bela goes to the garden to help Dadaji, who loves gardening. Bela’s parents also help each other with cooking, cleaning, and shopping for groceries. Banku and Bela give daily help to their grandparents, and children in the family learn from relatives and neighbours.
activities.prompt: Munni shows Bela colours made from dried flowers. What could Bela learn from this family friend?
options: She could learn that dried flowers can be turned into colours.
She could learn that colours are made by chopping vegetables.
She could learn that hair oil is made from dried flowers.
She could learn that garden soil is used to make colours.

why.She could learn that colours are made by: Chopping vegetables is a cooking task.
why.She could learn that hair oil is made fr: Hair oil is used on Bela’s hair.
why.She could learn that garden soil is used: Soil is part of garden work.

activities.explanation: Munni uses dried flowers to make colours.

activities.prompt: Explain how the family members help one another at home and in the garden.
activities.answer: Family members help by sharing daily work. Bela’s parents support each other with cooking, cleaning, and shopping. Banku cleans and chops vegetables, Bela assists Dadaji in the garden, and both children also help their grandparents. Dadiji supports Bela by oiling and braiding her hair.
points: The parents share housework.
Banku helps with cleaning and vegetables.
Bela helps Dadaji in the garden.
The children also help their grandparents.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: On a holiday, everyone went to the park with Dadaji. Many friends played pitthoo, calling to one another as they ran fast and placed stones quickly. Bela and her friends joined and made two teams. Dadaji scattered stones with a ball. The players ran to pile up the stones, while Rohit, Niku and Ronnie tried to hit the other team. After about twenty minutes, Dadaji bought everyone icecream. When it became dark, they went home.
activities.prompt: If Dadaji had not scattered the stones with the ball, what would the players be unable to do?
options: Collect the stones that Dadaji had sent out with the ball
Hit the other team because no teams had been made
Call to one another because the game had stopped
Buy icecream because the stones stayed in one place

why.Hit the other team because no teams had: Bela and her friends made two teams, so the teams could try to hit each other.
why.Call to one another because the game had: The players called to one another during the game, whatever happened to the stones.
why.Buy icecream because the stones stayed i: Dadaji bought icecream after about twenty minutes; scattering stones did not cause that.

activities.explanation: Dadaji used the ball to scatter the stones for the players to pile up.

activities.context: On a holiday, everyone went to the park with Dadaji. Many friends played pitthoo, calling to one another as they ran fast and placed stones quickly. Bela and her friends joined and made two teams. Dadaji scattered stones with a ball. The players ran to pile up the stones, while Rohit, Niku and Ronnie tried to hit the other team. After about twenty minutes, Dadaji bought everyone icecream. When it became dark, they went home.
activities.prompt: If the group was still at the park when it became dark, what should they do according to the story?
options: Head back home
Keep playing until Dadaji scatters more stones
Begin another game with different teams
Stay at the park until the next day

why.Keep playing until Dadaji scatters more: The story does not say that Dadaji scattered more stones or continued the game.
why.Begin another game with different teams: Making another game would not follow what happened in the story.
why.Stay at the park until the next day: They did not remain at the park overnight; they left when it became dark.

activities.explanation: The group went home after it became dark.

options: People care for one another
People live near many shops
Children only learn from books

chapters.title: Going to the Mela
chapters.summary: In this chapter: preparing for the mela; getting ready to leave; on the way to the mela; at the mela.

lessons.title: Preparing for the Mela

activities.prompt: Will Dadiji come along to the mela with everyone?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Getting Ready for the Mela
activities.body: The mela has finally come to town. Nita and Radha are getting ready to visit it, and everyone feels excited. The mela is a little far from their home. Dadiji asks why they are busy. Nita and Radha invite him, and Dadiji’s mother asks him to come too. Dadiji says his legs hurt, but he agrees after asking about water bottles.
keyPoints: The mela has come to town.
Nita and Radha are getting ready.
Dadiji agrees after asking about water bottles.
activities.explanation: The mela has arrived, and Dadiji agrees to join after asking about water bottles.

activities.prompt: Will Dadiji join Nita and Radha at the far mela?
steps: Dadiji’s mother asks him to come, so he thinks about joining.
The mela is far and his legs hurt, so he needs care.
Nita’s father promises that the group will look after him.
Dadiji asks about the water bottles, then agrees to come.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Who Is Getting Ready?
activities.prompt: Who is getting ready to go to the mela?
options: Nita and Radha
Dadiji and his mother
Sneha and Mohan Chacha
Radha and Nita's father
activities.explanation: Nita and Radha are the two people getting ready to go to the mela.

activities.title: How Far Is the Mela?
activities.prompt: The mela is very near their home.
activities.explanation: The mela is a little far from their home, so this statement is false.

activities.title: Why Are They Busy?
activities.prompt: Dadiji asks the others why they seem so ______.
activities.hint: This word describes what the others seem to be doing.
activities.explanation: Dadiji asks why the others seem so busy.

activities.title: Why Does Dadiji Agree?
activities.prompt: Why does Dadiji finally agree to come?
options: After speaking with his mother
After hearing the train arrive
After asking about water bottles
After helping carry the bottles
activities.explanation: Dadiji agrees only after he asks about the water bottles.

activities.title: Dadiji’s Steps
activities.prompt: Put Dadiji's steps in order.
items: Dadiji asks about the water bottles
activities.explanation: Dadiji is invited first. He asks about water bottles before agreeing to come.

activities.title: Nita’s Father’s Promise
activities.prompt: Which detail best shows Nita's father will care for Dadiji?
options: He says Dadiji should stay at home
He says the mela is very near home
He promises to care for Dadiji
He asks Dadiji to leave his bottles
activities.explanation: A promise to look after Dadiji directly shows that Nita’s father will care for him.

activities.prompt: The mela is a little far from home. Dadiji says his legs hurt. What will happen next?
options: Dadiji will stay home because his legs hurt.
Dadiji will join after asking about water bottles.
Dadiji will ask Nita’s father to stay home.
Dadiji will go alone without asking for help.

why.Dadiji will stay home because his legs h: This wrongly assumes leg pain alone will make Dadiji refuse.
why.Dadiji will ask Nita’s father to stay ho: This wrongly assumes Dadiji will ask Nita’s father to stay.
why.Dadiji will go alone without asking for: This wrongly assumes Dadiji will ignore the group’s help.

activities.explanation: Dadiji agrees after asking about the water bottles.

activities.prompt: Dadiji’s legs hurt, and Nita’s father will look after him. Why does Dadiji finally agree?
options: The group will care for him during the far trip.
The mela has suddenly become very close to home.
His legs will heal as soon as the trip starts.
He can reach the mela without anyone else’s help.

why.The mela has suddenly become very close: This wrongly assumes the distance to the mela has changed.
why.His legs will heal as soon as the trip s: This wrongly assumes the trip will heal Dadiji’s legs.
why.He can reach the mela without anyone els: This wrongly assumes Dadiji will not need the group’s care.

activities.explanation: The promised care helps Dadiji feel safer about going.

activities.prompt: Dadiji asks about the water bottles before agreeing to join the mela. Why does he ask?
options: He wants to know if water is available for the trip.
He wants the water bottles to stay at home.
He wants to carry every bottle by himself.
He thinks water can make his legs stop hurting.

why.He wants the water bottles to stay at ho: This wrongly assumes he does not want the water bottles.
why.He wants to carry every bottle by himsel: This wrongly assumes he expects to carry every bottle.
why.He thinks water can make his legs stop h: This wrongly assumes water will cure his leg pain.

activities.explanation: He asks first because he wants to know about water for the trip.

activities.prompt: Dadiji is invited, but the mela is far from home. Why does he say that his legs hurt?
options: He is worried about the trip to the far mela.
He wants the others to stop getting ready.
He expects his legs to heal at the mela.
He wants to go to the mela alone.

why.He wants the others to stop getting read: This wrongly reads his pain as a wish to stop the mela.
This wrongly assumes the mela will cure his leg pain.
This wrongly assumes leg pain means he wants to travel alone.

activities.explanation: Dadiji’s leg pain makes him worry about travelling so far.

activities.prompt: Nita’s father promises the group will look after Dadiji. Which plan is fairest for Dadiji?
options: Ask about water, then join the group that will care.
Go alone and carry all the water bottles.
Stay home while the group goes to the mela.
Leave before the group and travel alone to the mela.

why.Go alone and carry all the water bottles: This wrongly assumes Dadiji should carry everything alone.
why.Stay home while the group goes to the me: This wrongly assumes Dadiji cannot join the caring group.
why.Leave before the group and travel alone: This wrongly assumes Dadiji should travel before and alone.

activities.explanation: This plan uses the promised care and answers Dadiji’s water question.

lessons.title: Getting Ready to Leave

activities.prompt: How will everyone get ready for the exciting mela?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Ready for the Mela
activities.body: Nita says the special bag is ready. The children jump with joy. Everybody is happy because Dadiji has agreed to come. Nita’s father calls the neighbours. Mohan Chacha will meet them at the mela. Mohan Chacha’s family will meet Nita’s family at the mela. They will travel by a city bus. They take an autorickshaw to the mela ground. Radha says many people are going.
keyPoints: Nita’s special bag is ready.
Dadiji has agreed to come.
City bus, then autorickshaw.
Both families meet at the mela.
activities.explanation: Everyone is excited and getting ready to leave for the mela.

activities.prompt: While getting ready to leave, how will Nita’s family reach the mela ground?
steps: They will ride a city bus because it is the first part of their trip.
They will take an autorickshaw next because it takes them to the mela ground.
Mohan Chacha’s family will meet Nita’s family at the mela because both families plan to be there.
The families need not travel together because their meeting place is the mela.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Who has agreed to come?
options: Dadiji
Mohan Chacha
Radha
The neighbours
activities.explanation: Everybody is happy because Dadiji has agreed to come.

activities.prompt: Nita says their special bag is ready.
activities.explanation: Nita tells everyone that their special bag is ready.

activities.prompt: Mohan Chacha will meet them at the ______.
activities.hint: Think of the place where they will meet.
activities.explanation: Mohan Chacha tells them that he will meet them at the mela.

activities.prompt: They will take an autorickshaw to the mela ground before travelling by a city bus.
activities.explanation: They travel by the city bus first. Then, they take an autorickshaw.

activities.prompt: Match each person or group with what they do.
pairs: Says the special bag is ready
activities.explanation: Each person has a special part in getting ready for the mela.

activities.prompt: Where will Mohan Chacha’s family meet Nita’s family?
options: At the mela
At Nita’s home
At the bus stop
At the neighbours’ houses
activities.explanation: Mohan Chacha’s family will meet Nita’s family directly at the mela.

activities.prompt: Dadiji says no instead of agreeing to come. How would the children most likely feel?
options: They would not jump with joy.
They would still jump with joy.
They would feel angry with Dadiji.
They would feel worried about the mela.

This ignores that Dadiji has said no.
Nothing says the children would be angry with Dadiji.
Nothing shows that a changed plan would make them worried.

activities.explanation: Their happiness depends on Dadiji agreeing to come.

activities.prompt: Mohan Chacha says he will meet them at the mela. The families will meet directly. Must they ride together?
options: No. They can meet directly at the mela.
Yes. They must share the same city bus.
Yes. They must share the same autorickshaw.
No. They can meet before reaching the mela.

Sharing a bus is not needed for a meeting at the mela.
why.Yes. They must share the same autoricksh: Sharing an autorickshaw is not needed for their planned meeting.
why.No. They can meet before reaching the me: The plan places their meeting at the mela, not before it.

activities.explanation: Their families are planned to meet directly at the mela.

activities.prompt: Nita’s family has finished the city bus ride. What should they do next?
options: An autorickshaw ride to the mela ground.
Another city bus ride to the mela.
A meeting with Mohan Chacha after that.
A meeting with Dadiji after that.

This repeats the bus instead of following the stated order.
Meeting Mohan Chacha is a plan, not the next transport.
Meeting Dadiji is not the next part of the journey.

activities.explanation: The autorickshaw takes them from the bus to the mela ground.

activities.prompt: Radha says many people are going with them. What can Nita expect on the way?
options: A busy group travelling towards the mela.
An empty group travelling towards the mela.
A group waiting after the mela.
A group leaving without the special bag.

why.An empty group travelling towards the me: An empty group does not match Radha’s comment.
Radha says they are going with them, not waiting later.
Her comment does not say that anyone leaves the bag behind.

activities.explanation: Many people going with them means the group will not be empty.

activities.prompt: Nita’s father calls out to the neighbours. Does this explain Mohan Chacha’s promise?
options: No. The reason for the call is not given.
Yes. The call makes Mohan Chacha promise to meet them.
Yes. The call is Mohan Chacha’s whole travel plan.
Yes. The call explains the city bus ride to the mela.

why.Yes. The call makes Mohan Chacha promise: Nothing says the call made Mohan Chacha give his promise.
why.Yes. The call is Mohan Chacha’s whole tr: Nothing says the call is Mohan Chacha’s travel plan.
why.Yes. The call explains the city bus ride: Nothing links the call with the city bus ride.

activities.explanation: The two facts are separate because no link between them is given.

activities.prompt: While getting ready to leave, Nita says the special bag is ready. Dadiji has not agreed to come. What can her family tell?
options: The bag is ready, but Dadiji’s coming is unsure.
The bag is ready, and Dadiji will surely come.
The bag is not ready, and Dadiji will not come.
The bag is ready, so everyone must now leave.

why.The bag is ready, and Dadiji will surely: A ready bag does not promise Dadiji’s agreement.
why.The bag is not ready, and Dadiji will no: This disagrees with Nita saying that the bag is ready.
why.The bag is ready, so everyone must now l: A ready bag does not mean that everyone can leave now.

activities.explanation: The bag is ready, but Dadiji’s agreement has not been given.

lessons.title: On the Way to the Mela

activities.prompt: What will they see and hear on their way to the mela?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Getting Ready for the Mela
activities.body: Sneha and Rohit are Nita’s neighbours and close friends. When Nita’s family arrives, Sneha gets ready and checks her things. Their father says it is time to leave. Soon, they leave for the mela and walk carefully, watching vehicles in both directions. Bus 401 stops, and Dadiji gets help onto it. Rohit’s father buys tickets and tells the children to keep their hands and head inside.
keyPoints: Sneha gets ready when Nita’s family arrives.
They leave for the mela and watch the moving vehicles.
The conductor and Nita’s father help Dadiji onto bus 401.
activities.explanation: This is what happens on the way to the mela.

activities.prompt: Nita's family is arriving. Sneha is almost ready and checks her things. What happens next?
steps: Sneha checks her things because she is almost ready.
Their father says leave because it is time to go.
They all leave for the mela together because it is time.
They watch both directions so their careful walk stays safe.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Who are Nita’s neighbours and close friends?
options: Sneha and Rohit
Nita and Dadiji
Sneha and Dadiji
Nita and Rohit
activities.explanation: Sneha and Rohit are Nita’s neighbours and close friends.

activities.prompt: Bus number ______ slowly stops.
activities.hint: Look for the bus number in the story.
activities.explanation: Bus 401 is the bus that slowly stops.

activities.prompt: Match each person with the correct action.
pairs: Announces that it is time to leave
Buys five full and four half tickets
activities.explanation: Each person does the matching action in the story.

activities.prompt: What is reserved on the bus?
options: A ticket for older people
A seat for older people
A seat for close friends
A ticket for close friends
activities.explanation: There is a seat reserved for older people.

activities.prompt: Put these events in the correct order.
items: Sneha checks that she has everything she needs
Their father announces that it is time to leave
They all leave for the mela
They walk carefully and watch the vehicles
activities.explanation: Sneha gets ready before everyone leaves for the mela.

activities.prompt: Who helps Dadiji get on the bus?
options: The conductor alone
Sneha and Rohit
The conductor and Nita’s father
Rohit’s father alone
activities.explanation: The conductor and Nita’s father help Dadiji get on the bus.

activities.prompt: Nita's family is arriving. Sneha is almost ready and checks her things. What will happen next?
options: Finish getting ready and leave with the family.
Keep packing and wait until the next day.
Stay behind while the others go to the mela.
Go to the mela without checking her things.

why.Keep packing and wait until the next day: This mistake thinks leaving can wait until another day.
why.Stay behind while the others go to the m: This mistake ignores that they all leave for the mela together.
why.Go to the mela without checking her thin: This mistake ignores Sneha's careful check before leaving.

activities.explanation: This follows because Sneha is almost ready and her father announces leaving.

activities.prompt: The family walks toward the mela. Vehicles move in both directions. Why do they walk carefully?
options: To cross the road safely and carefully.
To count every vehicle that passes them.
To make the bus stop sooner than usual.
To find a reserved seat for every child.

This mistake thinks watching traffic is only for counting vehicles.
This mistake thinks careful walking is meant to speed up the bus.
This mistake mixes up walking safely with finding seats.

activities.explanation: Walking carefully and watching both directions helps them stay safe.

activities.prompt: Bus number 401 slowly stops. What happens next?
options: The conductor and Nita's father help Dadiji.
The conductor makes Dadiji run to the bus.
Dadiji waits while the bus drives away.
Rohit's father closes the bus door first.

why.The conductor makes Dadiji run to the bu: This mistake thinks people should board a moving bus quickly.
This mistake ignores the help given when the bus stops.
why.Rohit's father closes the bus door first: This mistake gives the bus door action to Rohit's father.

activities.explanation: The story says both help Dadiji get onto the stopped bus.

activities.prompt: A seat is reserved for older people. A child says, 'That seat should be for children first.' Why is this claim flawed?
options: The seat is meant for older people, not children.
Children have the same right to use that seat.
The seat is only for people with full tickets.
The seat can be used by anyone who arrives first.

why.Children have the same right to use that: This mistake thinks all passengers have equal rights to reserved seats.
why.The seat is only for people with full ti: This mistake thinks ticket type decides who uses a reserved seat.
why.The seat can be used by anyone who arriv: This mistake thinks arrival order matters more than the reserved rule.

activities.explanation: The rule says the reserved seat is for older people.

activities.prompt: Rohit's father buys five full and four half tickets. How many tickets does he buy altogether?
options: Seven tickets altogether
Eight tickets altogether
Nine tickets altogether
Ten tickets altogether

why.Seven tickets altogether: Five full tickets plus four half tickets make nine.
why.Eight tickets altogether: This mistake counts only two of the four half tickets.
why.Ten tickets altogether: This mistake counts each of the four half tickets twice.

activities.explanation: This mistake counts only three of the four half tickets.

activities.prompt: Rohit's father says children must keep their hands and head inside. Why does he say this?
options: Their hands or head could hit passing vehicles.
Their hands would make the bus windows dirty.
Their head would stop the bus from moving.
Their hands would take older people's seats.

why.Their hands would make the bus windows d: This mistake thinks the rule is about keeping the bus clean.
why.Their head would stop the bus from movin: This mistake thinks a head outside could stop the bus.
why.Their hands would take older people's se: This mistake mixes up the safety rule with reserved seating.

activities.explanation: Hands and head outside could meet moving vehicles.

lessons.title: At the Mela

activities.prompt: What will the family discover at the lively mela together?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Welcome to the Mela
activities.body: The families reach the big parade ground where the mela is held. A map shows the ground at the entrance. A Lost and Found booth has volunteers. The children enjoy games, toys, sweets, rides and a magic show. Mohan Chacha and Rohit get a wheelchair for Dadiji. Before eating, the children wash their hands. After eating, they put all waste in the dustbin.
keyPoints: The mela is held on the big parade ground.
Children enjoy games, toys, sweets, rides and a magic show.
They wash their hands before eating and use the dustbin afterwards.
activities.explanation: This card shows the places, treats and important actions at the mela.

activities.prompt: Dadiji cannot walk far at the mela. What should Mohan Chacha and Rohit do?
steps: They reach the big parade ground for the mela.
Dadiji cannot walk far, so she needs help moving there.
They hurry to get a wheelchair because it helps Dadiji move.
So getting one quickly is the right choice for Dadiji.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where is the map of the mela ground?
options: Outside the parade ground
At the entrance
Beside the dustbin
Inside the Lost and Found booth
activities.explanation: The map of the mela ground is at the entrance.

activities.prompt: An ambulance, a police jeep and a fire engine are parked beside the map.
activities.explanation: Yes! These vehicles are parked beside the map.

activities.prompt: Who needs the wheelchair that Mohan Chacha and Rohit get?
options: Mohan Chacha
Rohit
Dadiji
A volunteer
activities.explanation: Mohan Chacha and Rohit hurry to get a wheelchair for Dadiji.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with its place, group or activity.
activities.explanation: Each pair shows where something is, or what it is linked with.

activities.prompt: The children enjoy the ______ show.
activities.hint: Think of the show the children enjoy.
activities.explanation: The children enjoy the magic show.

activities.prompt: Mohan Chacha tells the children to wash their hands after eating.
activities.explanation: He tells them to wash their hands before eating.

activities.prompt: Put these actions in the correct order.
items: Put all waste in the dustbin
activities.explanation: The children wash their hands before eating and use the dustbin afterwards.

activities.prompt: After eating at the mela, what should happen to the waste?
options: Put all waste beside the stalls
Keep the waste in their hands
Put all waste in the dustbin
Put waste in the Lost and Found booth
activities.explanation: They put all the waste in the dustbin after eating.

activities.prompt: The family reaches the big mela ground and wants its layout. What should they use?
options: They should use the entrance map.
They should use the Lost and Found booth.
They should use the stalls with games.
They should use the merry-go-round.

why.They should use the Lost and Found booth: This helps with lost things, not with the ground's layout.
Game stalls offer fun things, not a guide to the ground.
It is a ride, not a guide to the mela ground.

activities.explanation: The map shows the layout of the mela ground.

activities.prompt: The children are eating at the mela. Which actions fit before and after the meal?
options: Wash hands; put waste in dustbin.
Buy toys; enjoy the magic show.
Get wheelchair; visit Lost and Found.
Use map; look at ambulance.

Buying toys and watching a show are not meal rules.
A wheelchair and Lost and Found help with other needs.
A map and an ambulance do not describe the meal rules.

activities.explanation: Handwashing comes before eating, and waste goes in the dustbin afterward.

lessons.title: Sharing Experience: Kumbh Mela

activities.prompt: What brings so many people together beside the rivers?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What is Kumbh Mela?
activities.body: Kumbh Mela is the world’s biggest festival. It is also the largest gathering of people. The festival is held on the banks of rivers. Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari and Shipra are rivers. It happens once every 12 years. Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain are places where it is held.
keyPoints: Kumbh Mela is the world’s biggest festival.
It is held on river banks once every 12 years.
Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain are places where it is held.
activities.explanation: Kumbh Mela brings people together on river banks.

activities.prompt: A family wants to make a Kumbh Mela trip. How should they choose where and when?
steps: It is held on river banks, so they need a river place.
It comes once every twelve years, so they must follow that cycle.
Each listed place can host it, so any can guide the trip.
They should choose any host place and follow the next cycle.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: How Often Does It Happen?
activities.prompt: Which statement about Kumbh Mela is true?
options: Every year
Every 12 years
Only one place
No river banks
activities.explanation: Kumbh Mela is held once every 12 years.

activities.title: Fill in the Gap
activities.prompt: Kumbh Mela is held once every ______ years.
activities.hint: Think about how often the festival returns.
activities.explanation: Kumbh Mela is held once every 12 years.

activities.title: Where Is the Festival Held?
activities.prompt: Kumbh Mela is held on the banks of rivers.
activities.explanation: The festival is held on river banks, so this is true.

activities.title: Match Each Clue
activities.prompt: Match each item with its correct description.
pairs: One place where it is held
One river named in the lesson
activities.explanation: Haridwar is a place, Ganga is a river, and 12 years is the gap.

activities.title: Find the River Pair
activities.prompt: Which pair names only rivers where Kumbh Mela is held?
options: Ganga and Yamuna
Haridwar and Nashik
Prayagraj and Shipra
Ujjain and Godavari
activities.explanation: Ganga and Yamuna are rivers. The other pairs include places.

activities.title: Find the Place Pair
activities.prompt: Which pair lists only places where Kumbh Mela is held?
options: Ganga and Yamuna
Haridwar and Shipra
Nashik and Ujjain
Godavari and Prayagraj
activities.explanation: Nashik and Ujjain are both places where the festival is held.

activities.prompt: A guide by the Ganga says Kumbh Mela is here now. What should the guide check first?
options: Whether it is time for the festival.
Whether the river has any water.
Whether every river hosts a festival.
Whether the crowd is the largest ever.

This wrongly treats water as the condition for the festival.
This wrongly assumes every river hosts the festival.
This wrongly treats a big crowd as proof of the timing.

activities.explanation: The guide should check the twelve-year festival cycle, not only the river.

activities.prompt: A baby is born just after a Kumbh Mela. About when will the next one come?
options: When the baby is younger than twelve.
When the baby is nearly twelve.
When the baby is older than twelve.
When the baby is much older than twelve.

The next festival comes exactly twelve years after the last one.
This assumes a gap longer than twelve years.
This ignores the festival’s twelve-year cycle.

activities.explanation: This assumes a gap shorter than twelve years.

activities.prompt: A group plans a Kumbh Mela trip to Haridwar. Which plan follows the rules?
options: Visit during the festival, twelve years after their last visit.
Visit every year and expect the same festival.
Visit an indoor hall during a festival year.
Visit only when the festival is away from a river.

why.Visit every year and expect the same fes: Every year is wrong because the festival comes once every twelve years.
why.Visit an indoor hall during a festival y: An indoor hall misses the river-bank setting where it is held.
why.Visit only when the festival is away fro: Being away from a river breaks the river-bank rule.

activities.explanation: Haridwar can host it, and it returns on a twelve-year cycle.

activities.prompt: A class can visit Nashik, Prayagraj, Ujjain, or Haridwar. Which choice is fairest for Kumbh Mela?
options: Any of the four, because each is a host place.
Nashik, because it is the only place that can host.
Prayagraj, because festivals only happen in that place.
Ujjain, because it is not on a river bank.

why.Nashik, because it is the only place tha: Being a host place does not make Nashik the only one.
why.Prayagraj, because festivals only happen: Being near a river does not limit the festival to Prayagraj.
why.Ujjain, because it is not on a river ban: Ujjain is listed, so excluding it is not a fair choice.

activities.explanation: All four are named as places where Kumbh Mela is held.
