activities.context: The mela has come to town, and Nita and Radha are getting ready to go. Everyone is excited, although the mela is a little far from their home. Dadiji asks why they seem so busy. Nita and Radha invite him to join them, and his mother has asked him to come too. Dadiji says his legs hurt. Nita’s father says many people are going and promises they will look after Dadiji. After asking about water bottles, Dadiji agrees to come.
activities.prompt: If Dadiji’s legs did not hurt, how would his decision likely change?
options: He would have less reason to hesitate about joining the group.
He would ask his mother to stop him from coming.
He would insist that the group must stay at home.
He would decide that nobody needs to carry water bottles.

why.He would ask his mother to stop him from: His mother asked him to come, not stay home.
why.He would insist that the group must stay: Many people were going, so staying home was unlikely.
why.He would decide that nobody needs to car: Water bottles were still important to Dadiji.

activities.explanation: His legs hurting was a reason to hesitate.

activities.context: The mela has come to town, and Nita and Radha are getting ready to go. Everyone is excited, although the mela is a little far from their home. Dadiji asks why they seem so busy. Nita and Radha invite him to join them, and his mother has asked him to come too. Dadiji says his legs hurt. Nita’s father says many people are going and promises they will look after Dadiji. After asking about water bottles, Dadiji agrees to come.
activities.prompt: If Dadiji still had not heard about the water bottles, what would be the sensible next step?
options: Check about them before agreeing to travel.
Ask his father to promise again that they will look after him.
Tell everyone that water bottles are not needed.
Ask Nita and Radha to go without him.

why.Ask his father to promise again that the: A second promise would not answer his question about water.
why.Tell everyone that water bottles are not: He had asked about the bottles because they mattered.
He had already been invited and agreed to join them.

activities.explanation: Dadiji checked about them before agreeing to come.

activities.prompt: Why does Dadiji finally agree to come to the mela?
activities.answer: Dadiji agrees because Nita and Radha invite him, his mother has asked him to come, and Nita’s father promises that the group will look after him. His legs hurt, but knowing that many people are going and that he will be cared for helps him decide.
points: Nita and Radha invite Dadiji.
His mother asks him to come.
His father promises that the group will look after him.
He checks about the water bottles before agreeing.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Nita says that their special bag is ready. The children jump with joy, and everybody is happy because Dadiji has agreed to come. Nita’s father calls out to the neighbours. Mohan Chacha tells them that he will meet them at the mela, where his family will meet Nita’s family directly. They will travel to the mela by a city bus and then take an autorickshaw to the mela ground. Radha says that many people are going with them.
activities.prompt: Nita’s father calls out to the neighbours after Dadiji agrees to come. Why is he most likely doing this?
options: He wants them to know about the happy family plan.
He is asking them to bring a different vehicle.
He is telling them that Dadiji cannot join the group.
He is asking them to decide whether Nita’s bag is packed.

why.He is asking them to bring a different v: No request for another vehicle is mentioned.
why.He is telling them that Dadiji cannot jo: Dadiji has agreed to come, not refused.
why.He is asking them to decide whether Nita: The special bag is already ready.

activities.explanation: He is sharing the news about Dadiji’s agreement.

activities.context: Nita says that their special bag is ready. The children jump with joy, and everybody is happy because Dadiji has agreed to come. Nita’s father calls out to the neighbours. Mohan Chacha tells them that he will meet them at the mela, where his family will meet Nita’s family directly. They will travel to the mela by a city bus and then take an autorickshaw to the mela ground. Radha says that many people are going with them.
activities.prompt: If Dadiji had not agreed to come, how would the reason for the children’s joy change?
options: They would not jump with joy because Dadiji would not be coming.
They would still jump because the special bag is ready.
They would jump because Mohan Chacha has promised to meet them.
They would jump because many people are going to the mela.

why.They would still jump because the specia: The bag being ready does not replace Dadiji’s agreement.
why.They would jump because Mohan Chacha has: Mohan Chacha’s meeting plan is not the stated reason for their joy.
why.They would jump because many people are: The number of people going does not replace Dadiji’s agreement.

activities.explanation: Their joy is caused by Dadiji’s agreement to come.

activities.prompt: Explain how the two families plan to reach the mela ground.
activities.answer: Nita’s family and Mohan Chacha’s family will meet directly at the mela. They will first travel there by city bus. After the bus journey, they will take an autorickshaw to reach the mela ground. Thus, their journey has two stages: travelling on the bus and then using the autorickshaw.
points: The families will meet directly at the mela.
The first part of the journey is by city bus.
They will then take an autorickshaw.
The journey ends at the mela ground.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Sneha and Rohit are Nita’s neighbours and close friends. When Nita’s family arrives, Sneha’s mother tells Sneha to get ready, and Sneha checks that she has everything she needs. Their father says it is time to leave. Soon, they all head for the mela, walking carefully and watching vehicles in both directions. Bus number 401 stops. The conductor and Nita’s father help Dadiji get on. Rohit’s father buys tickets and warns the children about the window.
activities.prompt: After bus number 401 stops, what happens next?
options: They both give Dadiji help as she boards.
They ask Dadiji to board only after everyone else enters.
They have Dadiji wait beside the stopped bus.
They tell Dadiji to find another way to the mela.

why.They ask Dadiji to board only after ever: Wrong: Dadiji does not have to wait for everyone else.
why.They have Dadiji wait beside the stopped: Wrong: she is helped onto the stopped bus.
why.They tell Dadiji to find another way to: Wrong: she reaches the mela using this bus.

activities.explanation: Correct: the conductor and Nita’s father both help Dadiji board.

activities.context: Sneha and Rohit are Nita’s neighbours and close friends. When Nita’s family arrives, Sneha’s mother tells Sneha to get ready, and Sneha checks that she has everything she needs. Their father says it is time to leave. Soon, they all head for the mela, walking carefully and watching vehicles in both directions. Bus number 401 stops. The conductor and Nita’s father help Dadiji get on. Rohit’s father buys tickets and warns the children about the window.
activities.prompt: When Dadiji is on bus number 401 and a seat is reserved for older people, what is the best choice?
options: Have Dadiji use the reserved seat.
Let Dadiji choose any empty seat.
Ask Dadiji to give the reserved seat to a child.
Ask Dadiji to remain standing.

Wrong: Dadiji should use the seat kept for her age group.
why.Ask Dadiji to give the reserved seat to: Wrong: the reserved seat is meant for an older person.
Wrong: Dadiji has a reserved seat available.

activities.explanation: Correct: the seat is intended for older people.

activities.prompt: Explain why the children should follow Rohit’s father’s instruction about the window.
activities.answer: Rohit’s father tells the children not to put their hands or head out of the window. They should follow this instruction because vehicles are moving in both directions. Keeping their hands and head inside helps them act safely while travelling.
points: Rohit’s father gives the instruction.
Their hands must stay inside the window.
Their head must stay inside too.
They should follow the warning for safety.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Imagine a family is preparing for Kumbh Mela. They know that it is the world’s biggest festival and the largest gathering of people. It is held on riverbanks, including the banks of Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, and Shipra. The family visits Haridwar, while other visitors are at Prayagraj or Nashik. The gathering happens once every 12 years.
activities.prompt: The family has just attended Kumbh Mela in Haridwar. What can they expect about a return to that place?
options: Kumbh Mela can return to Haridwar after 12 years.
It can return to Haridwar as soon as the family wishes.
It can return to Haridwar only after many other festivals have passed.
It will never return to Haridwar.

why.It can return to Haridwar as soon as the: Waiting for 12 years fits the festival’s cycle.
why.It can return to Haridwar only after man: The festival’s timing cannot be changed by wishing.
A regular festival can happen again.

activities.explanation: Kumbh Mela is held once every 12 years.

activities.context: Imagine a family is preparing for Kumbh Mela. They know that it is the world’s biggest festival and the largest gathering of people. It is held on riverbanks, including the banks of Ganga, Yamuna, Godavari, and Shipra. The family visits Haridwar, while other visitors are at Prayagraj or Nashik. The gathering happens once every 12 years.
activities.prompt: A visitor says the festival is not being held in Haridwar, Prayagraj, or Nashik. Which place fits?
options: Ujjain
Haridwar
Prayagraj
Nashik

why.Haridwar: Haridwar is a festival place, but the visitor rules it out.
why.Prayagraj: Prayagraj is a festival place, but the visitor rules it out.
why.Nashik: Nashik is a festival place, but the visitor rules it out.

activities.explanation: Ujjain is one of the places where it is held.

activities.prompt: Explain why Kumbh Mela can bring many people together.
activities.answer: Kumbh Mela brings many people together because it is the world’s biggest festival and the largest gathering of people. It is held on the banks of rivers, where many people can come for the festival. These facts help explain why so many people attend it.
points: It is the world’s biggest festival.
It is the largest gathering of people.
It is held on riverbanks.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Going to the Mela

activities.title: Dadiji’s Trouble
activities.prompt: Why is Dadiji finding it hard to join the mela trip?
options: His legs hurt
His bag feels heavy
He feels hungry
He lost his shoes
activities.explanation: Dadiji says that his legs hurt.

activities.prompt: Sneha and Rohit are arriving by bus.
activities.explanation: Sneha, Rohit and Mohan Chacha’s family are arriving by train.

activities.title: Their Bus
activities.prompt: They will travel to the mela by a city ______.
activities.hint: Look for the transport named in the lesson.
activities.explanation: Nita’s family will travel to the mela by a city bus.

activities.title: Who Will Do What?
activities.prompt: Match each person or family with what they will do.
pairs: will meet them at the mela
activities.explanation: Each pair shows an action or plan mentioned in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Mohan Chacha’s family meets Nita’s family directly at the mela.
activities.explanation: Both families meet directly at the mela.

activities.title: Before the Food
activities.prompt: Before eating, Mohan Chacha tells the children to wash their ______.
activities.hint: You clean these before eating food.
activities.explanation: Mohan Chacha tells the children to wash their hands before eating.

activities.title: Fun at the Mela
activities.prompt: Match each mela activity with its example from the story.
pairs: Gol gappas, chaat, chhole kulche and hot jalebis
activities.explanation: The children enjoy shopping, rides, a magic show and tasty food.

activities.prompt: Kumbh Mela is held only at Haridwar.
activities.explanation: It is held in Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain.

chapters.title: Celebrating Festivals
chapters.summary: In this chapter: festival of flowers: a journey to the himalayas; reaching the village and having lunch; spring festivals and the beauty of nature; festivals, seasons and special foods.

lessons.title: Festival of Flowers: A Journey to the Himalayas

activities.prompt: What wonders will Rishi discover among the mountains’ colourful flowers?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Rishi's Mountain Journey
activities.body: Rishi is from Jammu and is travelling to the Himalayas with his parents. He is going to visit his Mama, Mami and his cousins. They live in a small village near the mountains. The family is travelling by bus, and Rishi enjoys the ride. Outside, he sees a beautiful view, colourful flowers and tall trees. The mountain roads have hairpin turns: bends that curve sharply back.
keyPoints: Rishi is travelling to the Himalayas by bus.
Colourful flowers cover the hills.
Hairpin turns curve sharply back.
activities.explanation: This journey takes you from Jammu to a mountain village.

activities.prompt: Rishi's family sees a sign saying Men at Work. Why might the bus driver move carefully?
steps: The sign tells drivers that workers may be nearby.
The family is travelling by bus, so the driver must watch the road.
Careful driving helps keep the workers safe.
The driver should move carefully around the work area.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: How is the family travelling to the Himalayas?
options: By train
By bus
On foot
By boat
activities.explanation: The family is travelling by bus. Rishi is enjoying the ride.

activities.prompt: Their small village is near the ______.
activities.hint: Think of the large land forms near their village.
activities.explanation: Mama, Mami and the cousins live in a village near the mountains.

activities.prompt: Rishi is travelling to the Himalayas with his parents.
activities.explanation: Rishi is travelling to the Himalayas with both parents.

activities.prompt: Match each clue with its correct detail.
pairs: a small village near the mountains
activities.explanation: Each detail helps you picture Rishi's journey from Jammu to the mountains.

activities.prompt: What can be seen far away on the journey?
options: Tall trees
Small signs
Buses
Houses
activities.explanation: Many kinds of tall trees can be seen far away.

activities.prompt: What covers the hills on the journey?
options: Sand
Snow
Colourful flowers
Ice
activities.explanation: The hills are covered with colourful flowers. They make the view beautiful.

activities.prompt: The mountain road has hairpin turns. Why should the driver slow down?
options: The road bends sharply here.
The road becomes much wider.
The flowers grow closer together.
The bus becomes very empty.

This mistake thinks a hairpin turn makes the road wider.
This mistake thinks the flowers affect the driver's speed.
This mistake thinks an empty bus means the driver should slow.

activities.explanation: A hairpin turn bends sharply, so slowing is sensible.

activities.prompt: A road sign says No Horn Please. What should the bus driver do?
options: The driver should stay quiet.
The driver should sound one horn.
The driver should sound two horns.
Every passenger should shout outside.

This mistake ignores the meaning of No Horn Please.
This mistake ignores the meaning of No Horn Please.
This mistake turns a rule for drivers into noise for passengers.

activities.explanation: The sign asks the driver not to sound the horn.

activities.prompt: A road sign says School Ahead. What might the driver need to watch for?
options: Children may be near the road.
Flowers may be near the road.
Workers may be near the road.
Trees may be near the road.

This mistake confuses a school sign with the flowered hills.
This mistake confuses a school sign with Men at Work.
This mistake confuses a school sign with the tall trees.

activities.explanation: School Ahead means children may be near the road.

activities.prompt: A road sign says Men at Work. Why might the driver move carefully?
options: Workers may be working there.
Passengers may be leaving there.
Flowers may be falling there.
Children may be racing there.

This mistake thinks Men at Work means people are leaving.
This mistake confuses workers with flowers on the hills.
This mistake confuses workers with children near a school.

activities.explanation: Men at Work means workers may be near the road.

activities.prompt: Rishi is enjoying the bus ride. Which detail best explains why?
options: The view outside is beautiful.
His cousins are riding with him.
The horn is very loud today.
The bus is parked beside hills.

This mistake thinks his cousins are travelling inside the bus.
This mistake thinks noise is the reason for his enjoyment.
This mistake confuses the moving bus ride with stopping.

activities.explanation: The beautiful view explains why Rishi enjoys the ride.

lessons.title: Reaching the Village and Having Lunch

activities.prompt: What will the family discover on their walk before sharing a delicious lunch?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: From the Bus Stop to Lunch
activities.body: The family reaches the bus stop near the village. Everyone gets down, and Mamaji receives them. They walk on a broad concrete road. Rishi sees colourful flowers and recognises roses, marigolds and hibiscus. Nonikaa says one flower is a tulip. Later, Mami calls the children for lunch. Everyone has haakh, a leafy vegetable, with hot rice.
keyPoints: The family reaches the bus stop near the village.
Rishi enjoys colourful flowers in the garden.
Lunch includes haakh with hot rice.
activities.explanation: This card follows the family's visit from the bus stop to lunch.

activities.prompt: Rishi sees an unusual flower in the village garden. Why does it fit this family visit?
steps: Rishi knows roses, marigolds and hibiscus, so the unusual flower surprises him.
He is amazed because its beauty is unusual.
Nonikaa says one flower is a tulip, which fits the Kashmir tulip festival.
Therefore, the unusual tulip makes sense during the Kashmir tulip festival.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where does the family stop near the village?
options: at the bus stop
in the flower garden
for lunch
at the tulip festival
activities.explanation: The family reaches the bus stop near the village.

activities.prompt: They first walk on a broad ______ road.
activities.hint: Choose the material named for this road.
activities.explanation: They first walk on a broad concrete road.

activities.prompt: Match each place or time with the correct detail.
pairs: Rishi recognises roses, marigolds and hibiscus
everyone has haakh with hot rice
the family has a Kashmir tulip festival
activities.explanation: Each detail matches the place or time connected with it.

activities.prompt: Who tells Rishi that one flower is a tulip?
options: Nonikaa
Mami
Mamaji
Rishi
activities.explanation: Nonikaa tells Rishi that one flower is a tulip.

activities.prompt: Put the family's visit in order.
items: Have lunch with haakh and hot rice
activities.explanation: The family arrives, walks towards the garden and then has lunch.

activities.prompt: Which sentence uses one flower and one lunch food correctly?
options: Nonikaa names a tulip, and everyone eats haakh.
Rishi recognises rice, and Mami serves hibiscus.
Mamaji receives roses, and Nonikaa eats marigolds.
Everyone gets down, and haakh calls the children.
activities.explanation: Nonikaa names a tulip. Everyone has haakh with hot rice.

activities.prompt: The bus reaches the village stop. Everyone gets down. What will happen next?
options: Mamaji will receive the family at the stop.
Mamaji will make the family wait at the stop.
Mamaji will ask the family to stay on the bus.
Mamaji will walk away from the family at once.

why.Mamaji will make the family wait at the: This mistakes receiving them for making them wait.
why.Mamaji will ask the family to stay on th: This ignores that everyone has already got down.
why.Mamaji will walk away from the family at: This mistakes receiving them for leaving them.

activities.explanation: Mamaji receives them after they get down.

activities.prompt: Rishi knows roses, marigolds and hibiscus. He sees an unusual flower. What should he do?
options: Ask Nonikaa because she can name the unusual flower.
Pull the unusual flower out of the garden.
Eat the unusual flower before having lunch.
Walk past the unusual flower without looking.

why.Pull the unusual flower out of the garde: Pulling it shows no fair way to learn its name.
why.Eat the unusual flower before having lun: This mixes up the garden flower with the lunch.
why.Walk past the unusual flower without loo: This ignores his need to learn the flower's name.

activities.explanation: Nonikaa tells him that one flower is a tulip.

activities.prompt: Nonikaa says one garden flower is a tulip. Why is Rishi amazed?
options: He does not know it, and its beauty is unusual.
It stands beside the broad concrete village road.
It is eaten with haakh and the hot rice.
It welcomes Mamaji beside the village bus stop.

why.It stands beside the broad concrete vill: This mistakes where they walk for where the flowers are.
This mistakes a garden flower for a leafy vegetable.
why.It welcomes Mamaji beside the village bu: This treats a flower like a person who welcomes someone.

activities.explanation: Rishi is amazed by unusual beauty and hears its new name.

activities.prompt: Mami calls the children in for lunch. What will the children do next?
options: They will go in to eat the good-tasting lunch.
They will keep looking at the colourful flowers.
They will wait for the bus to leave again.
They will walk back to the village road.

why.They will keep looking at the colourful: This ignores Mami's call to come for lunch.
why.They will wait for the bus to leave agai: They have already got down, so they do not wait for the bus.
This mistakes walking to the road for going to lunch.

activities.explanation: Mami calls them in, and the meal tastes very good.

activities.prompt: A child says, “Our lunch is only hot rice.” Which correction is fair?
options: Rice, haakh and a Kashmiri dish are all served.
Only haakh is served, because the hot rice is separate.
Only the Kashmiri dish is served, because haakh is separate.
Only rice is served, because the other foods are separate.

why.Only haakh is served, because the hot ri: This thinks haakh is separate, but it is served with hot rice.
why.Only the Kashmiri dish is served, becaus: This thinks the Kashmiri dish is separate, but it is for lunch.
why.Only rice is served, because the other f: This thinks both extra foods are separate, but both are lunch.

activities.explanation: Everyone has haakh with rice and a Kashmiri dish for lunch.

activities.prompt: The family reaches the village during the Kashmir tulip festival. What links the visit and the unusual flower?
options: A tulip in the garden fits the Kashmir tulip festival.
Haakh and rice make the tulip look unusual.
The bus ride makes the tulip look unusual.
The concrete road makes the tulip grow colourful.

why.Haakh and rice make the tulip look unusu: This confuses a lunch cause with a flower cause.
why.The bus ride makes the tulip look unusua: This confuses travel with the reason for the flower.
why.The concrete road makes the tulip grow c: This mistakes the road for the place where tulips grow.

activities.explanation: The family has a Kashmir tulip festival at this time.

lessons.sceneAlt: Tulips are shown in full bloom at the Tulip Garden in Kashmir in April 2013.
lessons.sceneCaption: Colourful tulips bloom in rows at the Tulip Garden in Kashmir.

lessons.title: Spring Festivals and the Beauty of Nature

activities.prompt: What makes spring so colorful, joyful, and full of surprises?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Spring Is a Celebration
activities.body: Spring is a celebration of nature. The sun shines brightly after harsh winters. Flowers, grass and new leaves appear. Lovely red buransh flowers bloom at Rishi’s place. People place mustard and buransh flowers at their doorsteps. In Kerala, Unni’s family celebrates Vishu with yellow amaltas flowers. They also use fruits and vegetables for Vishu Kani.
keyPoints: Spring brings flowers, grass and new leaves.
Buransh flowers are also called Rhododendron.
Vishu uses yellow amaltas flowers, fruits and vegetables.
activities.explanation: Spring brings beautiful changes, colourful flowers and joyful festivals.

activities.prompt: After a harsh winter, a child visits Rishi's place and sees red flowers. Why is this a celebration of nature?
steps: The sun shines after harsh winters, so spring follows the cold time.
These red flowers are buransh, which bloom at Rishi's place in spring.
Spring brings flowers, grass and new leaves, so nature grows again.
The song hopes this brings cheer, so spring celebrates nature for everyone.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Flowers at Rishi’s Place
activities.prompt: Which flowers bloom at Rishi’s place in spring?
options: Mustard flowers
Red flowers
Yellow amaltas
Green grass
activities.explanation: Rishi’s place has lovely red flowers in spring. These are buransh flowers.

activities.title: Another Flower Name
activities.prompt: These spring flowers are called buransh or ______.
activities.hint: Look at the two names for the spring flower.
activities.explanation: These spring flowers are called buransh or Rhododendron.

activities.title: Flowers and Festival
activities.prompt: Match each item with its place or use.
activities.explanation: The pairs show spring flowers, doorstep decorations and Vishu Kani.

activities.title: What Makes Vishu Kani?
activities.prompt: What else is used to make Vishu Kani besides yellow amaltas flowers?
options: Fruits and vegetables
Mustard and buransh flowers
The harsh winter
The bright sunshine
activities.explanation: Vishu Kani uses fruits and vegetables too. Yellow amaltas flowers are also used.

activities.title: Why Spring Feels Joyful
activities.prompt: Why can spring feel like a celebration after harsh winters?
options: The elders give sweets
The sun shines brightly
The flowers stay hidden
The grass never grows
activities.explanation: Spring is described as a celebration of nature. Bright sunshine follows harsh winters.

activities.title: The Song’s Hope
activities.prompt: What does the song hope will happen?
options: Spring will bring harsh winter
Spring will bring yellow flowers
Spring will bring cheer to everyone
Spring will make everyone eat sweets
activities.explanation: The song hopes that spring will bring cheer to everyone.

activities.prompt: The harsh winter is ending, and the sun shines brightly. At Rishi's place, what is likely to bloom?
options: Red buransh flowers, because spring brings lovely flowers.
Yellow amaltas flowers, because they belong at every doorstep.
Green grass, because grass is called buransh.
No flowers, because the harsh winter continues.

why.Yellow amaltas flowers, because they bel: This confuses Vishu flowers with the flowers that bloom at Rishi's place.
why.Green grass, because grass is called bur: This mixes up grass with the name of a spring flower.
why.No flowers, because the harsh winter con: This overlooks that spring follows the harsh winter.

activities.explanation: This is right because lovely red buransh flowers bloom there in spring.

activities.prompt: Spring brings flowers, grass and new leaves. Which plan best checks whether new leaves appear in spring?
options: Look at the same tree before and after spring.
Look at one tree in spring and another in winter.
Look for leaves only after the spring song ends.
Count flowers instead of checking for leaves.

why.Look at one tree in spring and another i: Changing the tree makes the comparison unfair.
why.Look for leaves only after the spring so: Checking only after spring does not show that leaves appeared.
why.Count flowers instead of checking for le: This checks flowers instead of the new leaves in the question.

activities.explanation: This is fair because the same tree is checked before and after spring.

activities.prompt: Spring brings flowers, grass and new leaves. Rishi's place has red buransh flowers. A child says, “Spring is only about flowers.” What does this claim miss?
options: Grass and new leaves, because spring brings more than flowers.
Sweets and elders, because they also belong to spring.
Yellow flowers only, because all spring flowers are yellow.
Doorsteps, because people place flowers there.

why.Sweets and elders, because they also bel: This confuses the elders' blessing custom with the beauty of nature.
why.Yellow flowers only, because all spring: This wrongly believes that all spring flowers are yellow.
why.Doorsteps, because people place flowers: This names a place for flowers instead of the signs the claim misses.

activities.explanation: This is right because the claim misses the grass and new leaves.

lessons.sceneCaption: A Vishu Kani arrangement includes yellow konna flowers, rice, lemon, cucumber, betel leaves, arecanut, a mirror, and a holy text.

lessons.title: Festivals, Seasons and Special Foods

activities.prompt: Which festivals and special foods belong to the seasons people celebrate around the world?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Seasons, Festivals and Foods
activities.body: This lesson is about seasons, festivals and special foods. The seasons named here are spring, summer, monsoon and winter. The festival list includes Bihu, Holi, Chhath Puja and Onam. It also includes Christmas, Ugadi and Eid-ul-Fitr. The food list includes Thekua, Pitha, Plum Cake, Gujiya, Sadya, Holige and Seviyan.
keyPoints: Seasons: spring, summer, monsoon and winter
Festivals: Bihu, Holi, Chhath Puja, Onam, Christmas, Ugadi and Eid-ul-Fitr
Foods: Thekua, Pitha, Plum Cake, Gujiya, Sadya, Holige and Seviyan
activities.explanation: This card helps you remember the three groups named in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Cards are for seasons, festivals, and foods. What goes on each board?
steps: Spring, summer, monsoon, and winter belong to the seasons table.
Bihu, Holi, Chhath Puja, Onam, Christmas, Ugadi, and Eid-ul-Fitr are festivals.
Thekua, Pitha, Plum Cake, Gujiya, Sadya, Holige, and Seviyan are foods.
Matching each card to its list keeps every group correct.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Find the Festival
activities.prompt: Which one is a festival named in this lesson?
options: Pitha
Bihu
Winter
Sadya
activities.explanation: Great choice! Bihu appears in the festival list.

activities.title: Two Festival Names
activities.prompt: Christmas and Ugadi are both festival names.
activities.explanation: Yes! Both Christmas and Ugadi appear in the festival list.

activities.title: Choose the Festival Group
activities.prompt: Which pair contains only festival names?
options: Thekua and Pitha
Spring and summer
Bihu and Holi
Sadya and Gujiya
activities.explanation: Excellent! Bihu and Holi are both festival names.

activities.title: Complete the Food List
activities.prompt: The food list includes ______, Pitha and Plum Cake.
activities.hint: This food name starts with T.
activities.explanation: Well done! Thekua is included in the food list.

activities.title: Match Each Group
activities.prompt: Match each word with its group.
activities.explanation: Spring is a season, Bihu is a festival, and Thekua is a food.

activities.title: Order the Seasons
activities.prompt: Put the seasons in the order shown on the concept card.
activities.explanation: The seasons are shown as spring, summer, monsoon and winter.

activities.title: Foods or Seasons?
activities.prompt: Thekua and Pitha are both season names.
activities.explanation: Good try! Thekua and Pitha are foods, not seasons.

activities.title: The Festival Group
activities.prompt: Which group contains only festival names?
options: Thekua, Pitha and Gujiya
Spring, summer and winter
Sadya, Holige and Seviyan
Bihu, Holi and Onam
activities.explanation: Perfect! Bihu, Holi and Onam all appear in the festival list.

activities.prompt: A child sorts Holi and Holige cards. Which card goes with foods?
options: Holi card
Holige card
Bihu card
Onam card

why.Holi card: Holi is listed as a festival, so it does not go with foods.
why.Bihu card: Bihu is listed as a festival, so it does not go with foods.
why.Onam card: Onam is listed as a festival, so it does not go with foods.

activities.explanation: Holige is listed as food, so this is the correct card.

activities.prompt: A child wants equal food and festival cards. Which set has equal groups?
options: Thekua, Pitha, Bihu, Holi
Bihu, Holi, Chhath Puja, Onam
Seviyan, Holige, Plum Cake, Gujiya
Thekua, Bihu, Holi, Onam

why.Bihu, Holi, Chhath Puja, Onam: All these names are festivals, so the groups are not equal.
why.Seviyan, Holige, Plum Cake, Gujiya: All these names are foods, so the groups are not equal.
why.Thekua, Bihu, Holi, Onam: One food and three festivals make unequal groups.

activities.explanation: It has equal food and festival names, so the groups match.

lessons.sceneCaption: A traditional Husori troupe in vibrant attire performs the folk dance of Rongali Bihu in Assam.

lessons.title: Our Journey, the Roads and the Himalayas

activities.prompt: What stories do the mountains and roads tell us about the world around us?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: From Our Village to Mount Everest
activities.body: Chiya and Nonikaa live in a village near the mountains. A narrow mud road runs near their house. Red spring flowers are called buransh. Haakh is a leafy vegetable eaten with hot rice. The Himalayas lie in northern areas of India, and their name means "home of snow". Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world. It lies in Nepal and is about 8,848 metres high.
keyPoints: Chiya and Nonikaa live in a village near mountains.
The road near their house is a narrow mud road.
The Himalayas mean home of snow, and Mount Everest lies in Nepal.
activities.explanation: These ideas connect your village, its road, food, flowers and mountains.

activities.prompt: A child sees a mountain peak drawn above Mount Everest. Is the drawing correct?
steps: Mount Everest is the highest mountain peak in the world.
A peak above Everest would be higher than Everest.
This would contradict the fact that Everest is highest.
So the drawing cannot be correct under the given facts.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Road Near the House
activities.prompt: Which road is near Chiya and Nonikaa's house?
options: A narrow mud road
A wide mud road
A narrow stone road
A wide stone road
activities.explanation: The road near the house is narrow and made of mud.

activities.prompt: The red spring flowers are called buransh.
activities.explanation: Buransh is the name for the red spring flowers.

activities.title: The Height of Everest
activities.prompt: Mount Everest is about ______ metres high.
activities.hint: It is the highest mountain peak in the world.
activities.explanation: Mount Everest is about 8,848 metres high.

activities.title: Match Each Clue
activities.prompt: Match each clue to its correct name or place.
activities.explanation: Each clue points to its matching flower, vegetable, mountain range or country.

activities.title: The Meaning of Himalayas
activities.prompt: What does the name Himalayas mean?
options: home of flowers
home of rivers
home of snow
home of hills
activities.explanation: The name Himalayas means home of snow.

activities.title: Where Are the Himalayas?
activities.prompt: The Himalayas lie in the southern areas of India.
activities.explanation: The Himalayas lie in northern India, not southern India.

activities.title: The Country of Mount Everest
activities.prompt: Mount Everest lies in ______.
activities.hint: This country is named in the lesson.
activities.explanation: Mount Everest lies in Nepal, according to the lesson.

activities.prompt: A narrow mud road is by Chiya's house. Which vehicle fits more easily?
options: A small vehicle fits more easily.
A wide bus fits more easily.
A long truck fits more easily.
A wide cart fits more easily.

A wide bus may not fit because the road is narrow.
A long truck may struggle because the road is narrow.
A wide cart may struggle because the road is narrow.

activities.explanation: This is right because a small vehicle needs less room.

activities.prompt: A mountain is about 8,848 metres high. Which claim is supported?

activities.title: Celebrating Sarhul
activities.body: Sarhul is a spring festival celebrated in Jharkhand. People wear traditional clothes and walk in a procession to the sakhua tree. They carry freshly germinated grains, which means newly sprouted grains, and sakhua flowers. Offerings are made to the Earth and the Sun with reverence and gratitude. People sing and dance together. Drums such as dhol and nagada set the tune. Other local musical instruments are also used.
keyPoints: Sarhul is celebrated during spring in Jharkhand.
People carry newly sprouted grains and sakhua flowers.
Offerings show reverence and gratitude.
People sing, dance and play local instruments.
activities.explanation: Sarhul brings together spring, traditional dress, processions, offerings, music and dance.

lessons.title: Many Kinds of Plants and Trees

activities.prompt: What shapes and surprises will we discover among plants and trees?

activities.title: Plants and trees around us
activities.body: Plants around us come in many different sizes and shapes. Some leaves feel rough, while others feel smooth. A jamun tree may have thick, shiny leaves and tiny white flowers. Jamun fruits can change from green to red, then purple. A tree has a trunk of wood, many branches, and roots that grow deep into the soil. Leaves grow on its branches.
keyPoints: Plants have many sizes and shapes.
Jamun trees have special leaves, flowers and fruits.
A tree has a trunk, branches and roots.
activities.explanation: The trunk is the big wooden part. Branches spread out and carry leaves. Roots grow deep into the soil.

A rough surface feels different from a smooth surface.

activities.explanation: A tree has a big trunk of wood. Its branches spread out with leaves. Its roots go deep into the soil.

activities.title: Meet the shrubs
activities.body: Shrubs are medium-sized plants with several stems. Bushy-looking plants are called shrubs. A shrub may not have a big trunk like a tree. It can have many brown and woody stems. The woody stems and branches grow close to the ground. Some shrubs have pretty flowers. A tulsi plant at home can be a shrub.

They have several stems.
Their woody stems and branches grow close to the ground.

activities.hint: Look for the word used with brown stems.
activities.explanation: Shrub stems can be brown and woody. Great spotting!

activities.prompt: What can a shrub have instead of one big trunk?
options: pretty flowers
a tulsi home
several stems
brown branches
activities.explanation: Shrubs are medium-sized plants with several stems. Well done!

activities.prompt: Match each shrub clue with its matching description.
pairs: may not have a big trunk
activities.explanation: You matched each shrub clue correctly. Great work!

activities.prompt: A medium-sized plant has several stems. Its woody stems and branches grow close to the ground. What is this plant?
options: a tall tree
a shrub
one soft stem
a big trunk
activities.explanation: Its size, stems and branches show that it is a shrub. Excellent!

activities.prompt: Neha's home plant is medium-sized, has several stems and is bushy-looking. It is a ______.
activities.hint: Use the lesson word for a bushy-looking plant.
activities.explanation: A medium-sized, bushy-looking plant with several stems is a shrub.

activities.prompt: A small garden plant stays medium-sized and grows many woody stems close to the ground. What will it most likely look like?
options: It will look bushy, with several stems.
It will look like one tall tree trunk.
It will have only one soft green stem.
It will grow taller than every tree.

A shrub may not have one tall tree trunk.
A shrub can have many stems, not only one.
Not all plants grow as tall as trees.

activities.explanation: This matches the bushy shape and several stems of a shrub.

activities.prompt: At home, your tulsi has several stems close to the ground. Why can it be a shrub?
options: Its bushy shape and several stems fit a shrub.
It must have a tall trunk, just like a tree.
It must be taller than every other plant.
It must have only one soft green stem.

why.It must have a tall trunk, just like a t: The mistake is thinking a shrub must have a tall trunk.
why.It must be taller than every other plant: A shrub is medium-sized, not taller than every plant.
The mistake is thinking a shrub has only one stem.

activities.explanation: The bushy shape and several stems fit a shrub.

activities.prompt: You want to check if a bushy plant is a shrub. Which test is fair?
options: Check its size, woody stems, and low growth.
Check only if it has pretty flowers.
Check only if it grows taller than a tree.
Check only if it has one very big trunk.

The mistake is thinking pretty flowers prove a plant is a shrub.
why.Check only if it grows taller than a tre: A shrub does not need to grow taller than a tree.
A shrub may not have one very big trunk.

activities.explanation: Size, woody stems, and low growth are useful shrub signs.

activities.prompt: A plant has pretty flowers. Its height and stem shape have not been checked. What can we say?
options: It might be a shrub, but flowers alone cannot tell.
It must be a shrub because it has pretty flowers.
It cannot be a shrub because it has flowers.
It must be a tree because it has pretty flowers.

why.It must be a shrub because it has pretty: The mistake is thinking every flowering plant is a shrub.
why.It cannot be a shrub because it has flow: The mistake is thinking flowers rule out being a shrub.
why.It must be a tree because it has pretty: The mistake is thinking pretty flowers make a plant a tree.

activities.explanation: Some shrubs have pretty flowers, but this alone cannot prove it.

activities.prompt: Maya says, “Every plant with many branches is a tree.” Which observation shows her claim is wrong?
options: A bushy plant has several stems close to the ground.
A tree has many branches high above the ground.
A tall plant has its leaves near the top.
A small plant has just one soft green stem.

why.A tree has many branches high above the: The mistake is thinking tall branches make every plant a tree.
why.A tall plant has its leaves near the top: The mistake is thinking leaves near the top prove it is a tree.
why.A small plant has just one soft green st: The mistake is thinking one stem means a plant cannot have branches.

activities.explanation: A bushy plant with several low stems can be a shrub.

activities.prompt: Your tulsi is medium-sized with several woody stems. It has no big trunk. Is it a shrub?
options: Yes, because its size and stems fit a shrub.
No, because every shrub has a big trunk.
No, because shrubs cannot have woody stems.
Yes, because every medium plant is a tree.

The mistake is thinking every shrub needs a big trunk.
why.No, because shrubs cannot have woody ste: The mistake is thinking shrubs cannot have woody stems.
why.Yes, because every medium plant is a tre: The mistake is thinking all medium-sized plants are trees.

activities.explanation: Its medium size and several woody stems fit a shrub.

lessons.title: Herbs and Grasses

activities.prompt: What do mint, bamboo, and wheat have in common?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet Herbs and Grasses
activities.body: Herbs have tender stems. These stems stay soft instead of becoming woody. Herbs are smaller plants. Grasses are types of herbs. Grass leaves are thin and flat, while grass stems are hollow. Many different kinds of grasses exist. Sugarcane and bamboo are tall grasses. Bamboo is a special kind of grass. It stays alive for longer than one year. The grains we eat are seeds of large grasses.
keyPoints: Herbs are smaller plants.
Their stems stay soft.
Grasses are types of herbs.
Grass leaves are thin and flat.
Grass stems are hollow.
activities.explanation: This shows how herbs and grasses are alike and different.

activities.prompt: In a garden, how can we sort mint, tomato, sugarcane, and bamboo?
steps: Mint and tomato can have soft stems, so they can be herbs.
Herbs have tender stems that never become woody, so this fits them.
Sugarcane and bamboo are tall grasses, so they form the grass group.
Grasses are types of herbs, so both groups belong inside herbs.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which feature helps us call a plant an herb?
options: Soft stems
Thin leaves
Hollow stems
Woody stems
activities.explanation: Herbs have tender stems that do not become woody. Soft stems match this description.

activities.prompt: Mint and tomato plants can have soft and green stems.
activities.explanation: Mint and tomato plants can have soft and green stems. You remembered this correctly.

activities.prompt: Plants with tender stems that do not become woody are called ______.
activities.hint: This word names smaller plants with soft stems.
activities.explanation: Herbs have tender stems. These stems do not become woody.

activities.prompt: Match each plant or plant part with its special feature.
activities.explanation: Each pair matches a special feature from your book. Grasses have thin, flat leaves and hollow stems.

activities.prompt: Which statement about grass leaves is true?
options: Their leaves are thin and flat.
Their leaves are broad and round.
Their leaves are thick and curved.
Their leaves are short and woody.
activities.explanation: Your book tells us that grass leaves are thin and flat. So the first choice is correct.

activities.prompt: The grains we eat are whole grass plants.
activities.explanation: The grains we eat are seeds of large grasses. They are not whole grass plants.

activities.prompt: Put these ideas in order from the plant to the food.
activities.explanation: Large grasses provide the seeds. Those seeds are the grains we eat.

activities.prompt: Which plant is a tall grass that lives for longer than one year?
options: Bamboo
Sugarcane
Mint plant
Tomato plant
activities.explanation: Bamboo is a tall grass. It also stays alive for longer than one year.

activities.prompt: Which check would best show that a plant is a grass?
options: Look for thin, flat leaves and a hollow stem.
Check whether the stem stays soft for many years.
Look for a tall stem and a very long life.
Check whether the plant gives large grass seeds.

why.Check whether the stem stays soft for ma: Softness points to herbs, not to these grass features.
why.Look for a tall stem and a very long lif: Height and long life do not show every grass feature.
why.Check whether the plant gives large gras: Large seeds belong to large grasses, not all grasses.

activities.explanation: Thin, flat leaves and hollow stems are grass features.

activities.prompt: A gardener keeps bamboo for years. What does this show?
options: Bamboo is a special grass with long life.
Bamboo is a tall grass with a short life.
Bamboo is an ordinary grass with one-year life.
Bamboo is a tall plant without grass features.

why.Bamboo is a tall grass with a short life: This wrongly calls bamboo's life short.
why.Bamboo is an ordinary grass with one-yea: This wrongly limits bamboo to one year of life.
why.Bamboo is a tall plant without grass fea: This ignores bamboo's special grass type and long life.

activities.explanation: Bamboo is a special grass and lives longer than one year.

lessons.title: Climbers and Creepers

activities.prompt: How do plants get support as they grow taller and wider?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Climbers and Creepers
activities.body: Climbers and creepers both have thin, flexible stems. Climbers grow by climbing other plants for support. Some climbers take their food from the plant they climb. Creepers grow by creeping along the ground. A money plant cannot stand alone. It climbs a wall, but creeps along the ground without support.
keyPoints: Climbers need support from other plants.
Creepers grow along the ground.
Climbers and creepers have thin, flexible stems.
activities.explanation: These plants grow in different ways, but they have similar stems.

activities.prompt: A money plant is beside a wall. Will it stand alone or climb?
steps: It cannot stand alone, so it needs something for support.
A wall is beside it, so it has something to climb.
It can spread upwards, so it can grow higher on the wall.
Therefore, it will slowly climb the wall instead of standing alone.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: A Climbing Money Plant
activities.prompt: What can a money plant slowly climb?
options: A wall
The ground
A tall tree
A pumpkin plant
activities.explanation: A money plant can spread upwards and slowly climb a wall.

activities.title: The Money Plant's Stem
activities.prompt: A money plant has a long and ______ stem.
activities.hint: This stem bends easily.
activities.explanation: The money plant has a long, thin stem.

activities.title: Match Each Plant
activities.prompt: Match each plant with its special way of growing.
activities.explanation: Each plant has a special way of growing and moving.

activities.title: Support for Climbers
activities.prompt: How do climbers get support?
options: By climbing other plants
By standing alone
By creeping on the ground
By spreading branches
activities.explanation: Climbers grow by climbing other plants for support.

activities.title: Without Something to Climb
activities.prompt: What does a money plant do when it has nothing to climb?
options: It creeps on the ground
It winds up a tree
It spreads branches on ground
It stands up alone
activities.explanation: A money plant creeps along the ground when it has nothing to climb.

activities.title: A Climber's Food
activities.prompt: Some climbers take their ______ from the plant on which they climb.
activities.hint: You eat this kind.
activities.explanation: Some climbers take their food from the plant on which they climb.

activities.prompt: A money plant cannot stand alone and has nothing to climb. What will this creeper do?
options: It will creep along the ground.
It will climb up into the air.
It will grow a thick, strong stem.
It will stand upright by itself.

This wrongly thinks it can climb without any support.
This wrongly expects its thin stem to become thick.
This ignores that the money plant cannot stand alone.

activities.explanation: With nothing to climb, this creeper creeps along the ground.

activities.prompt: A thin, flexible vine grows beside a tall tree. How will this climber grow?
options: It will wind up the tree for support.
It will creep along the ground below.
It will spread branches along the ground.
It will grow a thick and strong stem.

This confuses a climbing vine with a creeper.
why.It will spread branches along the ground: This mistakes a pumpkin plant's spreading for a vine.
This wrongly thinks climbers need thick, strong stems.

activities.explanation: A vine can wind up a tall tree for support.

activities.prompt: A pumpkin plant grows in open ground. How will this creeper spread?
options: They will spread along the ground.
They will climb up a tall tree.
They will wind around a nearby wall.
They will stand up by themselves.

This mistakes a pumpkin creeper for a climber.
This mistakes a pumpkin creeper for a climbing vine.
This wrongly treats a creeper as a plant that stands alone.

activities.explanation: A pumpkin plant spreads its branches along the ground.

activities.prompt: A money plant has a long, thin stem beside a wall. How will this climber grow?
options: It will slowly climb up the wall.
It will creep far along the ground.
It will wind up a tall tree.
It will grow a thick, strong stem.

This confuses wall climbing with ground creeping.
This confuses the money plant with a vine.
This wrongly expects its thin stem to become thick.

activities.explanation: A money plant can spread upwards and slowly climb a wall.

activities.prompt: A child says, “A money plant will always climb upwards.” Which comparison is fair?
options: Put one money plant by a wall and one on the ground.
Put both money plants by the same tall tree.
Put both money plants on the same bare ground.
Put one money plant by a wall and one by a tree.

why.Put both money plants by the same tall t: Both can climb, so this cannot compare climbing with creeping.
why.Put both money plants on the same bare g: Neither has support, so this cannot compare climbing with creeping.
why.Put one money plant by a wall and one by: Both have support, so this cannot compare climbing with creeping.

activities.explanation: This compares climbing with creeping, so it tests the claim.

lessons.title: Leaves and Plant Friends

activities.prompt: What might we discover by noticing a plant’s leaves?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Notice Your Plant Friends
activities.body: Plants can have leaves with different colours, shapes and sizes. While observing, you can check whether leaves, flowers and fruits are many, few or absent. New leaves can grow, and leaf colours can change as they grow larger. Old brown leaves can fall. You can describe leaves by colour, shape, size, texture and smell. Mint and lemon grass have different smells.
keyPoints: New leaves can grow, while old brown leaves can fall.
Leaf colours can change as leaves grow larger.
Colour, shape, size, texture and smell help describe leaves.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you observe leaves carefully and describe them clearly.

activities.prompt: A plant has many leaves, few flowers, and no fruits. What can change?
steps: The child records many leaves, few flowers, and absent fruits.
This shows the plant now because all three plant parts are checked.
New leaves can grow, while flowers or fruit can appear later.
So the record can change because the plant can change.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Different Leaves
activities.prompt: Which sentence matches what your book says about leaves?
options: Different plants can have leaves of different sizes.
Different plants always have leaves of the same size.
All plants have leaves of the same shape.
Leaves can only have one possible colour.
activities.explanation: Your book says that different plants can have leaves with different sizes.

activities.title: Smell a Leaf
activities.prompt: Rubbing a ______ leaf helps us notice its smell.
activities.hint: This leaf can come from a fruit tree.
activities.explanation: Rubbing a mango leaf helps us notice its smell.

activities.prompt: Old brown leaves can fall to the ground.
activities.explanation: Old brown leaves can fall to the ground.

activities.title: What Can You Record?
activities.prompt: What can you record while observing a plant?
options: Record if leaves, flowers and fruits are many, few or absent
Record if leaves and flowers are always present on every plant
Record if flowers and fruits are always present on every plant
Record if leaves, flowers and fruits always have one number
activities.explanation: The lesson tells us to record whether these plant parts are many, few or absent.

activities.title: Describe a Leaf
activities.prompt: Which words list every way to describe a leaf?
options: Colour, shape, size, texture and smell
Colour, shape, size, fruit and smell
Colour, shape, fruit, texture and smell
Colour, fruit, size, texture and smell
activities.explanation: These are all the features listed for describing leaves.

activities.title: Track Leaf Changes
activities.prompt: Which plan best records changes in leaves?
options: Track new leaves, colour changes and fallen leaves
Track new leaves, flower changes and fallen leaves
Track new leaves, colour changes and fruit changes
Track new leaves, colour changes and texture changes
activities.explanation: New leaves can grow, colours can change and old brown leaves can fall.

activities.prompt: A plant has leaves but no flowers. What might happen later?
options: Its leaves must all fall away.
Its leaves must stay exactly the same.
Flowers or fruit can appear on it.
The plant can never grow again.

The facts do not say all leaves must fall away.
New leaves can grow, and leaf colours can change.
A plant can grow new leaves and show new flowers or fruit.

activities.explanation: says flowers or fruit can appear on a plant.

activities.prompt: Mint and lemon grass smell different. How should a child compare them?
options: Smell each leaf and notice the difference.
Smell one leaf and assume both match.
Choose leaves by colour and skip smelling.
Use size alone to guess their smells.

It wrongly assumes the second leaf matches the first.
why.Choose leaves by colour and skip smellin: Colour cannot show how these two leaves smell.
Size alone cannot reveal the different leaf smells.

activities.explanation: says mint and lemon grass have different smells.

activities.prompt: A mango leaf has a colour. Can its colour show its smell?
options: Yes, colour shows what every leaf smells like.
Yes, darker leaves always have stronger smells.
No, rub the leaf to notice its smell.
Yes, colour shows how strong the leaf's smell is.

why.Yes, colour shows what every leaf smells: Colour can describe a leaf, but it cannot show smell.
why.Yes, darker leaves always have stronger: The facts do not connect darker colour with stronger smell.
why.Yes, colour shows how strong the leaf's: The facts do not connect leaf colour with smell strength.

activities.explanation: says rubbing lets the child notice a mango leaf's smell.

lessons.title: Parts of a Plant and Bark

activities.prompt: What wonders might a tree reveal if we look closely?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Plants and Their Bark
activities.body: The main parts of a plant are roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds. Bark is the hard outer covering of a tree trunk. You may see animals, insects or plants on it. A crayon or pencil can copy a bark pattern on paper. The pattern can help you guess which tree it came from.
keyPoints: Roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds are the main plant parts.
Bark is the hard outer covering of a tree trunk.
Animals, insects or plants may be seen on tree bark.
A bark pattern can help you guess which tree it came from.
activities.explanation: This card introduces plant parts and the bark around a tree trunk.

activities.prompt: A child finds bark on a tree. How can it help?
steps: The tree trunk's hard outer covering is bark.
A crayon or pencil can copy that bark pattern onto paper.
The copied pattern can help guess which tree it came from.
So, the paper pattern is a useful clue to the bark.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which one is a main part of a plant?
options: Bark
Sugar
Roots
Umbrella
activities.explanation: Roots are one of the main parts of a plant.

activities.prompt: A crayon or pencil can make a pattern of tree ______ on paper.
activities.hint: It is the hard outside covering of a tree trunk.
activities.explanation: A crayon or pencil can copy tree bark on paper.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with its correct description.
pairs: Hard outer covering of a tree trunk
Biggest flower, as big as an umbrella
Place where the Rafflesia is found
activities.explanation: Each description matches the plant or place named on the left.

activities.prompt: What can a bark pattern help you do?
options: Guess which tree it came from
Guess which animal lived there
Guess when the tree grew
Guess how tall it was
activities.explanation: A bark pattern can help you guess which tree it came from.

activities.prompt: Where is the Rafflesia flower found?
options: Mizoram
On tree bark
In sugar cane
Under an umbrella
activities.explanation: A Rafflesia flower is found in Mizoram.

activities.prompt: Which statement about bamboo or the Rafflesia is true?
options: Rafflesia is the tallest kind of grass.
Bamboo is the tallest kind of grass.
Bamboo is the biggest kind of flower.
Rafflesia is the biggest kind of grass.
activities.explanation: Bamboo is the tallest kind of grass.

activities.prompt: One child copies bark in blue. Another copies it in green. Which comparison is fair?
options: Compare the bark patterns, not the crayon colours.
Compare only blue, because blue fits bark better.
Compare only green, because green fits bark better.
Compare neither, because crayon colour hides patterns.

why.Compare only blue, because blue fits bar: This wrongly thinks the crayon colour must match the bark.
why.Compare only green, because green fits b: This wrongly thinks the crayon colour must match the bark.
why.Compare neither, because crayon colour h: This wrongly thinks crayon colour hides a bark pattern.

activities.explanation: Each bark pattern can help guess which tree it came from.

activities.prompt: A child calls bark a drawing. They say animals cannot be seen there. What is the best correction?
options: Bark is hard, and animals may be on it.
Bark is soft, and animals stay away.
Bark is hard, but animals are only inside.
Bark is soft, and plants may be on it.

This confuses hard bark with a soft drawing.
why.Bark is hard, but animals are only insid: This puts animals inside instead of on the bark surface.
Plants may be seen on bark, but calling bark soft is wrong.

activities.explanation: Bark is a hard outer covering, and animals may be seen on it.

activities.prompt: A child sees fruit with seeds inside. Which plant parts are seen?
options: Fruits and seeds
Bark and roots
Leaves and flowers
Stems and bamboo

why.Bark and roots: The scene shows fruit and seeds, not bark and roots.
why.Leaves and flowers: The scene shows fruit and seeds, not leaves and flowers.
why.Stems and bamboo: Bamboo is a kind of grass, not the fruit or seed seen.

activities.explanation: Fruits and seeds are both main parts of a plant.

activities.prompt: A child says sugar comes from bark. Which part really gives sugar?
options: The sugar cane stem
The bamboo stem
The Rafflesia flower
The tree bark

why.The bamboo stem: This confuses bamboo's grass clue with the sugar clue.
why.The Rafflesia flower: This confuses the biggest flower with the sugar source.
why.The tree bark: This repeats the mistake that bark produces sugar.

activities.explanation: Sugar is produced from the sugar cane stem.

activities.prompt: A gardener wants the tallest kind of grass. What should they choose?
options: The bamboo plant
The Rafflesia flower
The sugar cane stem
The tree bark

why.The Rafflesia flower: This confuses the biggest flower with the tallest grass.
why.The sugar cane stem: This confuses the sugar-making stem with the tallest grass.
why.The tree bark: This confuses the trunk's hard covering with the tallest grass.

activities.explanation: Bamboo is the tallest kind of grass.

activities.prompt: A child in Mizoram finds a flower as big as an umbrella. Which flower fits?
options: The Rafflesia flower
The bamboo plant
The sugar cane stem
The tree bark

why.The bamboo plant: This confuses the tallest grass with the biggest flower.
why.The sugar cane stem: This confuses the sugar-making stem with the biggest flower.
why.The tree bark: This confuses the trunk's hard covering with the biggest flower.

activities.explanation: The Rafflesia is found there and is as big as an umbrella.

lessons.title: Test practice
lessons.sceneAlt: A jamun tree shows dense foliage, smooth glossy oval leaves, rough brownish-gray bark, and branches spreading wide.
lessons.sceneCaption: A jamun tree with glossy oval leaves and wide-spreading branches.

activities.context: A student goes for a walk beside a jamun tree and looks at it from the trunk to the branches. The trunk is big and made of wood, while the roots go deep down into the soil. Leaves grow along the spreading branches. The student touches and smells the leaves. Tiny white flowers grow on the tree, and a green jamun fruit hangs nearby.
activities.prompt: The student stays beside the tree as the green fruit changes. What color sequence should the student expect?
options: Red first, and purple later.
Purple first, and red later.
Red first, with no later change.
No color change will occur.

This reverses the stated order of the color change.
The fruit can continue changing after it turns red.
Jamun fruits are able to change color.

activities.explanation: Jamun fruits can change from green to red and then purple.

activities.context: A student goes for a walk beside a jamun tree and looks at it from the trunk to the branches. The trunk is big and made of wood, while the roots go deep down into the soil. Leaves grow along the spreading branches. The student touches and smells the leaves. Tiny white flowers grow on the tree, and a green jamun fruit hangs nearby.
activities.prompt: After touching the jamun leaves, which description should the student give?
options: Thick and shiny
Rough and shiny
Smooth and shiny
Rough and thick

why.Rough and shiny: Rough is not part of the jamun leaf description.
why.Smooth and shiny: Smooth is not part of the jamun leaf description.
why.Rough and thick: The leaves can be thick, but they are described as shiny rather than rough.

activities.explanation: Jamun leaves can be thick and shiny.

activities.prompt: Explain how leaves and roots are different and where they are found.
activities.answer: Leaves grow on branches that spread out from a tree's trunk. They can be touched and smelled, and their surfaces may feel rough or smooth. Roots are different because they grow down into the soil. A jamun tree can also have thick, shiny leaves.
points: Leaves are found on spreading branches.
Leaves may have rough or smooth surfaces.
Leaves can be touched and smelled.
Roots go deep down into the soil.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student examines a tulsi plant at home. It is medium-sized, with several stems and many brown, woody stems. Its branches grow close to the ground, and the plant looks bushy. It does not have a big trunk like a tree. Some of its stems have pretty flowers. The student wonders why it is called a shrub.
activities.prompt: Which explanation best fits why the plant has a shrub's shape?
options: It has several stems, with its woody growth staying low.
Its single tall stem explains the bushy form.
Its pretty flowers make its branches grow near the ground.
Its big trunk supports the plant's bushy shape.

why.Its single tall stem explains the bushy: The plant has several stems, not one stem.
why.Its pretty flowers make its branches gro: Pretty flowers do not explain why branches grow close to the ground.
why.Its big trunk supports the plant's bushy: The plant does not have a big trunk like a tree.

activities.explanation: Several stems and low woody growth match the description of a shrub.

activities.context: A student examines a tulsi plant at home. It is medium-sized, with several stems and many brown, woody stems. Its branches grow close to the ground, and the plant looks bushy. It does not have a big trunk like a tree. Some of its stems have pretty flowers. The student wonders why it is called a shrub.
activities.prompt: The student says, “This is a tulsi at home, so it cannot be a shrub.” Which response is best?
options: That doubt can be wrong, because a tulsi at home can be a shrub.
It is right, because a home tulsi must have a big trunk.
It is right, because shrubs never have pretty flowers.
It is right, because only trees can have woody stems.

why.It is right, because a home tulsi must h: A home tulsi does not have to have a big trunk.
why.It is right, because only trees can have: Shrubs have woody stems and branches.

activities.explanation: A tulsi plant at home can be a shrub.

activities.prompt: Explain how a shrub is different from a tree.
activities.answer: A shrub is medium-sized and has several stems, often brown and woody. Its woody stems and branches grow close to the ground, making it look bushy. A shrub may not have a big trunk like a tree. This shows how a shrub can be different from a tree without being tall.
points: A shrub is medium-sized.
It has several woody stems.
Its stems and branches grow close to the ground.
It may not have a big trunk like a tree.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A gardener plants mint and tomato beside tall sugarcane and bamboo. The mint and tomato have soft, green stems, so they are herbs. The gardener notices that the bamboo and sugarcane are grasses. Bamboo is a special kind of grass and stays alive for longer than just one year. The gardener also knows that grasses have thin, flat leaves and hollow stems. The grains eaten at lunch are seeds of large grasses.
activities.prompt: If the mint's soft green stem became woody, which classification would change?
options: The mint would no longer be an herb.
The mint would become a type of grass.
The tomato would stop being an herb.
The bamboo would stop being a special kind of grass.

Becoming woody would not make the mint a grass.
The change to the mint would not affect the tomato.
why.The bamboo would stop being a special ki: The change to the mint would not affect the bamboo.

activities.explanation: Herbs have tender stems that do not become woody.

activities.context: A gardener plants mint and tomato beside tall sugarcane and bamboo. The mint and tomato have soft, green stems, so they are herbs. The gardener notices that the bamboo and sugarcane are grasses. Bamboo is a special kind of grass and stays alive for longer than just one year. The gardener also knows that grasses have thin, flat leaves and hollow stems. The grains eaten at lunch are seeds of large grasses.
activities.prompt: If bamboo and sugarcane did not have hollow stems, what could still be true?
options: They would still be grasses.
They would no longer be grasses.
Bamboo would no longer be a special kind of grass.
Sugarcane would no longer be a tall grass.

Changing one feature would not undo the fact that both are grasses.
why.Bamboo would no longer be a special kind: Bamboo's special kind of grass status would not depend on its stem alone.
why.Sugarcane would no longer be a tall gras: Sugarcane's tall-grass classification would not be changed by its stem alone.

activities.explanation: The stated grass classification does not depend only on having hollow stems.

activities.prompt: Explain how an herb is different from a grass.
activities.answer: An herb is a smaller plant with soft stems that do not become woody. A grass is a type of herb. Grasses have thin, flat leaves and hollow stems. So grasses fit within the herb group, but not every herb has to be a grass.
points: Herbs are smaller plants.
Herbs have soft, non-woody stems.
Grasses are a type of herb.
Grasses have thin, flat leaves and hollow stems.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: At home, a money plant is placed beside a wall. Its long, thin stem cannot stand up by itself, so the stem slowly spreads upwards along the wall. Because it has something to climb, the money plant stays off the ground. Nearby, a pumpkin plant spreads its branches along the ground. Above them, a vine winds up a tall tree, using it for support and taking some food from it.
activities.prompt: If the wall is removed from beside the money plant, what would it most likely do next?
options: It would creep sideways along the ground.
It would stand upright by itself.
It would grow branches like a pumpkin plant.
It would wind up the nearby tree.

Its long, thin stem cannot support itself.
why.It would grow branches like a pumpkin pl: Spreading branches along the ground describes a pumpkin plant.
Winding up a tree describes a vine, not the money plant in the case.

activities.explanation: It has nothing left to climb, so it would creep along the ground.

activities.context: At home, a money plant is placed beside a wall. Its long, thin stem cannot stand up by itself, so the stem slowly spreads upwards along the wall. Because it has something to climb, the money plant stays off the ground. Nearby, a pumpkin plant spreads its branches along the ground. Above them, a vine winds up a tall tree, using it for support and taking some food from it.
activities.prompt: What best explains why the vine grows upward on the tree?
options: It uses the tree for support as a climber.
It cannot stand up by itself.
It spreads its branches along the ground.
It takes food from the tree, so it must climb.

That describes the money plant's need for support.
why.It spreads its branches along the ground: Spreading branches along the ground is creeper growth.
why.It takes food from the tree, so it must: Taking food from the plant is possible for some climbers, but it does not explain upward growth.

activities.explanation: Climbers grow upwards by using other plants for support.

activities.prompt: How do climbers and creepers grow in different ways?
activities.answer: A climber grows upward by using another plant for support, so the vine can wind up the tree. A creeper grows along the ground, so the pumpkin plant spreads its branches there. The money plant also needs something to climb because its long, thin stem cannot stand up by itself.
points: Climbers use other plants for support.
Creepers grow along the ground.
Climbers and creepers have thin, flexible stems.
The money plant cannot support itself.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A child visits a plant and records that its leaves are green, with different shapes and sizes. The leaves are many, the flowers are few, and no fruits are present. A new leaf is growing, and some older leaves look brown. The child rubs a mango leaf and notices a smell. Soon, an old brown leaf falls to the ground.
activities.prompt: What might happen to a leaf's colour as the plant grows?
options: The colour might change as the leaf grows larger.
The colour must change in exactly the same way for every leaf.
The colour cannot change after the child first sees it.
The colour changes only when the leaf becomes a fruit.

why.The colour must change in exactly the sa: The fact does not say every leaf changes in the same way.
why.The colour cannot change after the child: Leaves can change colour while growing.

activities.explanation: Leaf colours can change as leaves grow larger.

activities.context: A child visits a plant and records that its leaves are green, with different shapes and sizes. The leaves are many, the flowers are few, and no fruits are present. A new leaf is growing, and some older leaves look brown. The child rubs a mango leaf and notices a smell. Soon, an old brown leaf falls to the ground.
activities.prompt: What can be said about the smell of a mango leaf compared with mint and lemon grass?
options: It can be different because different leaves can have different smells.
It must be exactly the same as the smell of mint.
It must be exactly the same as the smell of lemon grass.
It cannot have any smell because leaves do not have smells.

why.It must be exactly the same as the smell: The fact does not say mango, mint and lemon grass smell the same.
The fact does not say mango, mint and lemon grass smell the same.
why.It cannot have any smell because leaves: Rubbing a mango leaf lets a child notice its smell.

activities.explanation: Different leaves can have different smells.

activities.context: During a visit, a child saw roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds. Sugar was produced from a sugar cane stem, while bamboo was the tallest kind of grass. In Mizoram, a Rafflesia flower was found. It was the biggest flower and as big as an umbrella. The child looked at a tree trunk and spotted an insect on its bark. A pencil made a bark pattern on paper, which helped the child guess which tree it came from.
activities.prompt: In the case, suppose the child changes from the pencil to a crayon. What can the child still make?
options: A pattern of tree bark on paper.
A pattern of the Rafflesia flower.
A pattern of the sugar cane stem.
A pattern of bamboo grass.

This would copy the Rafflesia rather than the tree bark in the case.
This would copy the sugar cane stem rather than the bark.
This would copy bamboo rather than the tree bark.

activities.explanation: Correct: either a crayon or a pencil can make a bark pattern on paper.

activities.context: During a visit, a child saw roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds. Sugar was produced from a sugar cane stem, while bamboo was the tallest kind of grass. In Mizoram, a Rafflesia flower was found. It was the biggest flower and as big as an umbrella. The child looked at a tree trunk and spotted an insect on its bark. A pencil made a bark pattern on paper, which helped the child guess which tree it came from.
activities.prompt: The child wants to point out the plant seen in Mizoram that is as big as an umbrella. What should the child point to?
options: The umbrella-sized Rafflesia
The tallest grass
The sugar-making stem
The trunk's hard outer layer

why.The tallest grass: Bamboo is the tallest kind of grass, not the umbrella-sized flower.
why.The sugar-making stem: The sugar cane stem is the part from which sugar is produced.
why.The trunk's hard outer layer: Bark is the hard outer covering of a tree trunk, not the umbrella-sized plant seen in Mizoram.

activities.explanation: Correct: the Rafflesia in Mizoram is as big as an umbrella.

activities.prompt: Explain how the bark pattern helps the child guess which tree it came from.
activities.answer: The child uses a crayon or pencil to make the bark pattern on paper. Bark is the hard outer covering of a tree trunk. The pattern can then help the child guess which tree it came from.
points: A crayon or pencil can make the pattern.
The pattern is made on paper.
Bark covers the outside of a tree trunk.
The pattern helps the child make a guess.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.
