activities.context: A family has brought an animal and a plant into their home. The animal has only just started living there. Sometimes the family is happy to share the home with them, but at first they feel scared because the animal is new. The family gives the animal and the plant water, food and shelter. They do not hurt the animal, even though they are scared, because animals usually do not hurt others unless they feel threatened by people.
activities.prompt: The family is scared of the animal. What should they do next?
options: Keep caring for it while making sure nobody causes it harm.
Make the animal leave by frightening it.
Stop giving it food until it stops frightening the family.
Hurt it so it learns to stay away from people.

Frightening it could make it feel threatened.
why.Stop giving it food until it stops frigh: It still needs food, as well as water and shelter.
why.Hurt it so it learns to stay away from p: Animals must not be hurt, even when people are afraid.

activities.explanation: Fear does not cancel the duty not to hurt animals.

activities.context: A family has brought an animal and a plant into their home. The animal has only just started living there. Sometimes the family is happy to share the home with them, but at first they feel scared because the animal is new. The family gives the animal and the plant water, food and shelter. They do not hurt the animal, even though they are scared, because animals usually do not hurt others unless they feel threatened by people.
activities.prompt: If the animal feels threatened by a person, what is likely to happen?
options: It may try to hurt the person because it feels threatened.
It will usually hurt the person because every animal in a home becomes dangerous.
It will stop needing food and shelter because it feels threatened.
It will be unable to hurt the person because it is being cared for.

why.It will usually hurt the person because: Animals are not automatically dangerous when they start living in a home.
why.It will stop needing food and shelter be: Feeling threatened does not remove the animal's need for water, food and shelter.
why.It will be unable to hurt the person bec: Being cared for does not mean an animal can never act when threatened.

activities.explanation: Animals usually do not hurt others unless they feel threatened by people.

activities.prompt: How should a family care for animals and plants that live in their home?
activities.answer: A family should give its animals and plants water, food and shelter. If family members do not like an animal or feel scared, they should still not hurt it. They should remember that animals usually do not hurt others unless people make them feel threatened.
points: Provides water, food and shelter.
Does not hurt animals when they are disliked.
Does not hurt animals when people are scared.
Remembers that threatened animals may hurt others.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Shambhu went through the forest with his father. They sat under the shade of a huge mango tree, which was home to birds, squirrels and monkeys. Shambhu saw a monkey eating a mango and throwing out the seed. A new plant would grow from that seed. A mango also dropped from the tree, and Shambhu picked it up. The scene shows how animals and plants help each other.
activities.prompt: What could happen after the monkey throws out the mango seed?
options: The seed could grow into a new plant.
The monkey could eat the seed instead.
The mango could turn into a new plant.
The seed could grow into a mango fruit.

The monkey had already eaten the mango and thrown out the seed.
The seed grows into a plant, not into the whole mango.
The seed grows into a plant, not into a fruit.

activities.explanation: The seed can grow into a new plant.

activities.context: Shambhu went through the forest with his father. They sat under the shade of a huge mango tree, which was home to birds, squirrels and monkeys. Shambhu saw a monkey eating a mango and throwing out the seed. A new plant would grow from that seed. A mango also dropped from the tree, and Shambhu picked it up. The scene shows how animals and plants help each other.
activities.prompt: A mango drops near Shambhu. What should he do, based on what happened in the case?
options: He should collect the mango from the ground.
He should leave the mango for the monkey.
He should throw the mango into the forest.
He should leave the mango where it falls.

why.He should leave the mango for the monkey: The case shows him collecting the fallen mango.
why.He should throw the mango into the fores: There is no reason in the case for him to throw it away.
why.He should leave the mango where it falls: The case shows him picking it up instead of leaving it.

activities.explanation: Shambhu picked up the mango when it dropped.

activities.prompt: Explain how the monkey and the mango tree help each other.
activities.answer: The monkey helps the plant by throwing out the seed after eating the mango. That seed can grow into a new plant. The mango tree helps the monkey by giving it fruit and a home among the other animals. This shows how animals and plants help each other.
points: The monkey eats a mango.
The monkey throws out the seed.
The seed can grow into a new plant.
The tree provides fruit and a home for animals.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A boy watches squirrels bury nuts in a garden. The squirrels later forget where they hid them, and thousands of trees are accidentally planted. The boy gives animals food and protects plants. He also sees animals dispersing seeds and making soil fertile, which helps plants grow and spread near and far. He knows that people and living things need one another.
activities.prompt: If the squirrels keep burying nuts and forgetting where they hid them, what could happen next?
options: More trees could be accidentally planted as squirrels leave nuts behind.
No trees could be planted because squirrels would take care of every nut.
Plants would spread more widely even if animals stopped helping them.
Only animal habitats would improve, while plant growth stayed the same.

why.No trees could be planted because squirr: Squirrels do not take care of every buried nut.
why.Plants would spread more widely even if: Animals help plants spread through seed dispersal.
why.Only animal habitats would improve, whil: The changes would affect plants as well as animals.

activities.explanation: Squirrels forget some hiding places, leaving nuts that can become trees.

activities.context: A boy watches squirrels bury nuts in a garden. The squirrels later forget where they hid them, and thousands of trees are accidentally planted. The boy gives animals food and protects plants. He also sees animals dispersing seeds and making soil fertile, which helps plants grow and spread near and far. He knows that people and living things need one another.
activities.prompt: After seeing animals help plants, what should the boy do to continue caring for both animals and plants?
options: Show compassion by giving the animals food and protecting them.
Stop giving food and protection because the animals no longer need help.
Keep the animals away from plants so the soil cannot change.
Care only for the plants and ignore the animals that help them.

why.Stop giving food and protection because: Animals still depend on people for food and shelter.
why.Keep the animals away from plants so the: Animals help make soil fertile for plants.
why.Care only for the plants and ignore the: Plants and animals depend on each other.

activities.explanation: Animals deserve kindness, care and compassion.

activities.context: A boy watches squirrels bury nuts in a garden. The squirrels later forget where they hid them, and thousands of trees are accidentally planted. The boy gives animals food and protects plants. He also sees animals dispersing seeds and making soil fertile, which helps plants grow and spread near and far. He knows that people and living things need one another.
activities.prompt: If fewer animals helped plants by dispersing seeds and making the soil fertile, what might happen?
options: Plants might grow and spread less widely.
Plants would grow faster because fewer animals would use the soil.
Animals would no longer need plants for food or shelter.
Plant growth would be unaffected because animals and plants do not depend on each other.

why.Plants would grow faster because fewer a: Healthy soil supports the growth of plants.
why.Animals would no longer need plants for: Animals and plants depend on each other for food and shelter.
why.Plant growth would be unaffected because: Animals and plants help each other in many ways.

activities.explanation: Seed dispersal and fertile soil help plants grow and spread.

activities.prompt: Why do people need animals and plants, and how do they help one another?
activities.answer: People and animals and plants need one another. People give animals and plants care, protection, food and shelter. Animals and plants give us food, shelter and clothing. Animals also help plants by dispersing seeds and making soil fertile, helping plants grow and spread near and far.
points: People give care, protection, food and shelter.
Animals and plants provide food, shelter and clothing.
Animals disperse seeds.
Animals make soil fertile so plants can grow and spread.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A student chose a sparrow because she often sees it around her. She observed it closely whenever she got the chance. She first saw it near her, and it was alone. The bird made sounds that surprised her and made her laugh. She wrote a short description and shared her story with her classmates.
activities.prompt: The student sees the sparrow again. What should she do next to learn more about it?
options: Write the story without looking at it.
Watch it closely and notice what it does.
Guess what it does without observing it.
Look at another animal instead.

This skips the chance to observe closely.
Guessing does not show that she observed closely.
Choosing another animal does not help her observe the sparrow.

activities.explanation: This helps her learn more about the sparrow.

activities.context: A student chose a sparrow because she often sees it around her. She observed it closely whenever she got the chance. She first saw it near her, and it was alone. The bird made sounds that surprised her and made her laugh. She wrote a short description and shared her story with her classmates.
activities.prompt: If the student had first seen the sparrow with its friends, what should she change in her story?
options: Say that the sparrow was not alone.
Say that the sparrow made no sounds.
Say that she did not see the sparrow.
Say that the sparrow was only one friend.

The case says that the bird made sounds.
The case says that she did see the sparrow.
why.Say that the sparrow was only one friend: The first sighting would involve the sparrow and its friends, not one friend.

activities.explanation: The first sighting would have included the sparrow's friends.

activities.prompt: How does observing an animal closely help the student write a description and tell her story?
activities.answer: Observing closely helps the student describe the animal she chose. She can notice what it looks like and what sounds it makes. Then she can write a short description and tell classmates when and where she first saw it, and whether it was alone or with friends.
points: Observes the chosen animal closely.
Describes what it looks like and the sounds it makes.
Includes when and where it was first seen.
Explains whether it was alone or with friends.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A child brings three small amounts of sugar, a papad and rice from the kitchen. The child places each food one foot apart, then watches as ants arrive. Some ants look different. An ant goes straight toward the sweet food, so the child notices which item the ants visit first. Later, the child feels sad and speaks to the plant friend.
activities.prompt: If the child accidentally moves two foods close together, what should the child do?
options: Separate the foods again, leaving one foot between each one.
Put all three foods together in one place.
Leave two foods touching while keeping the third food away.
Place one food directly on top of another food.

why.Put all three foods together in one plac: Putting the foods together does not follow the spacing rule.
why.Leave two foods touching while keeping t: There should also be one foot between these two foods.
why.Place one food directly on top of anothe: Stacking foods does not keep them one foot apart.

activities.explanation: The activity says to keep one foot of distance between the foods.

activities.context: A child brings three small amounts of sugar, a papad and rice from the kitchen. The child places each food one foot apart, then watches as ants arrive. Some ants look different. An ant goes straight toward the sweet food, so the child notices which item the ants visit first. Later, the child feels sad and speaks to the plant friend.
activities.prompt: If the child's feelings changed from sad to happy, what should the child do?
options: Speak with the plant while feeling happy.
Avoid speaking to the plant because it is only for sad feelings.
Wait until the child feels upset before speaking to the plant.
Talk to the plant only when the ants are nearby.

why.Avoid speaking to the plant because it i: The plant is not only for sad, upset or angry feelings.
why.Wait until the child feels upset before: There is no need to wait for an upset feeling before talking to the plant.
why.Talk to the plant only when the ants are: Talking to the plant does not depend on the ants being nearby.

activities.explanation: The child can talk to the plant when happy as well as when upset.

activities.prompt: How should the child arrange the foods, and what should the child watch while the ants visit?
activities.answer: The child should keep the three foods one foot apart because this is the proper arrangement for the activity. The child should then watch which food item the ants go to first. The child should also remember that the ants may not all look the same, so their appearances can be different.
points: Brings three small amounts of food
Keeps one foot of distance between the foods
Watches which food item the ants go to first
Remembers that the ants may look different
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: At school, children act like an animal while classmates guess it. After the game, they can switch roles. The lesson reminds them that people depend on plants and animals, and plants and animals also depend on us. The teacher shares a true story from Valparai, a small town in Tamil Nadu. There, children and teachers watch for birds, record them, and make welcome posters when Grey Wagtails arrive from the mountains. The birds are called Vaalatti kuruvi in Tamil.
activities.prompt: In the guessing game, what could happen when the class switches roles?
options: The original guesser could act like an animal while the partner guesses.
The original guesser could act like an animal while the partner only watches.
The original guesser and partner could both guess while no one acts.
The original guesser could name the animal while the partner copies the movements.

why.The original guesser could act like an a: Watching alone would not use the guessing role properly.
why.The original guesser and partner could b: Someone must act while another person guesses.
why.The original guesser could name the anim: Naming the animal before acting would take away the guessing game.

activities.explanation: Switching roles means the other partner becomes the guesser.

activities.context: At school, children act like an animal while classmates guess it. After the game, they can switch roles. The lesson reminds them that people depend on plants and animals, and plants and animals also depend on us. The teacher shares a true story from Valparai, a small town in Tamil Nadu. There, children and teachers watch for birds, record them, and make welcome posters when Grey Wagtails arrive from the mountains. The birds are called Vaalatti kuruvi in Tamil.
activities.prompt: If the children stopped recording the birds, what would they no longer have?
options: A clear list showing which birds visited the town.
A way to welcome Grey Wagtails from the mountains.
A record of how many posters the class put up.
A record of every animal the children guessed.

why.A way to welcome Grey Wagtails from the: Welcome posters and recording birds are different activities.
why.A record of how many posters the class p: The posters do not count how many were made.
why.A record of every animal the children gu: The guessing game involved acting, not recording animals.

activities.explanation: Recording birds shows which birds came to the town.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Living in Harmony

activities.title: The Monkey's Mango
activities.prompt: What was the monkey eating in Shambhu's story?
options: Eating a mango
Eating a nut
Drinking water
Playing with a squirrel
activities.explanation: The monkey ate a mango. It then threw out the seed.

activities.prompt: Animals usually hurt others only when they feel threatened by us.
activities.explanation: Animals usually stay peaceful unless they feel threatened by us.

activities.prompt: Shambhu saw a monkey eating a ______ and throwing out the seed.
activities.hint: It grows on a huge tree.
activities.explanation: The monkey was eating a mango. The seed could grow into a new plant.

activities.title: The Squirrel Story
activities.prompt: Put the squirrel story in order.
items: Squirrels forget where they hid them
Trees are accidentally planted by squirrels
activities.explanation: Hidden nuts help new trees grow. This is a helpful partnership between squirrels and plants.

activities.title: Helping Plants
activities.prompt: How do animals help plants?
options: By dispersing seeds and making soil fertile.
By giving us milk and loving company.
By giving us shade and fresh air.
By giving us wood for our houses.
activities.explanation: Animals spread seeds and make the soil fertile. This helps plants grow and spread.

activities.prompt: Squirrels always remember every place where they bury nuts.
activities.explanation: Squirrels bury nuts and forget where they hid them. New trees can grow from them.

activities.prompt: When you feel sad, upset or angry, talk to your ______ friend.
activities.hint: This living thing also needs your care and support.
activities.explanation: You can talk to your plant when you feel sad or upset. You can also talk to it when you are happy.

activities.title: The Valparai Story
activities.prompt: Match each part of the Valparai story with its detail.
activities.explanation: The children and teachers record visiting birds. They also welcome them with posters.

activities.title: Watch the Ants
activities.prompt: Put the ant-watching activity in order.
items: Keep one foot of distance between them
Watch which food the ants go to first
activities.explanation: The three foods can be sweet, fried, or boiled or cooked. Then watch the ants.

chapters.title: Water — A Precious Gift
chapters.summary: In this chapter: rain and where the water goes; water comes to our homes; water in daily lives and storing water; using water and saving every drop.

lessons.title: Rain and Where the Water Goes

activities.prompt: Where does rainwater go after it falls?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Where Rainwater Goes
activities.body: Rain sends water down to the ground. The water can soak into the ground, gather in puddles, or flow away. Some water flows under the soil and joins a stream or pond. A stream later joins a river. Water in wells comes from underground water.
keyPoints: Rain sends water down to the ground.
Rainwater can soak in, gather, or flow away.
Water in wells comes from underground water.
activities.explanation: Rainwater follows many paths on and under the ground.

activities.prompt: Heavy rain has fallen. Where can the rainwater go next?
steps: Rain sends much water down, so the ground receives rainwater.
Soaked water stays below, but flowing water reaches streams or ponds.
Some water gathers in puddles instead of moving onward.
Therefore, rainwater can take several paths after it falls.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Heavy or Light Rain
activities.prompt: The lesson says rain can be...
options: Big or small
Heavy or light
Clean or dirty
Underground or above
activities.explanation: Rain can be heavy or light. These words describe how much rain there is.

activities.title: Raindrop Sizes
activities.prompt: All raindrops are the same size.
activities.explanation: Raindrops can be big or small. They are not always the same size.

activities.title: Rainwater Collects
activities.prompt: Rainwater can soak into the ground, gather in ______, or flow away.
activities.hint: This is one place where rainwater gathers.
activities.explanation: Puddles are one place where rainwater gathers. Rainwater can also soak in or flow away.

activities.title: Collecting Rainwater
activities.prompt: What can you check about collected rainwater?
options: Whether it looks clean or dirty
Whether it feels heavy or light
Whether it feels big or small
Whether it moves straight or slants
activities.explanation: You can look at collected rainwater to see whether it looks clean or dirty.

activities.title: A Water Journey
activities.prompt: Put this water's journey in order.
items: The stream later joins a river
activities.explanation: This order shows one possible path for rainwater. Rainwater can take other paths too.

activities.title: Water in Wells
activities.prompt: Where does the water in wells come from?
options: From underground water
From water in puddles
From water in ponds
From water in lakes
activities.explanation: Wells get water from underground water stored under the ground.

activities.title: Water Under the Soil
activities.prompt: Some rainwater can flow under the soil and join a stream or pond.
activities.explanation: Yes. Rainwater can flow under the soil and join a stream or pond.

activities.prompt: The rain is light and its drops are small. What will it still do?
options: Pull water up from underground.
Send water down to the ground.
Keep all water in the air.
Move water into a river.

This mistake thinks well water pulls itself upward.
This mistake thinks light rain never reaches the ground.
This mistake treats rain as water already flowing in a river.

activities.explanation: says rain sends water down to the ground.

activities.prompt: A child claims that all rainwater is clean. What is the fair test?
options: Collect it under soil and look.
Watch it slant and change direction.
Let it flow into a pond.
Collect it in a vessel and look.

This mistake looks below ground instead of collecting rainwater.
This mistake checks direction instead of how the water looks.
This mistake checks flowing water instead of collected rainwater.

activities.explanation: says to collect rainwater and see if it looks clean or dirty.

lessons.title: Water Comes to Our Homes

activities.prompt: How does water find its way from nature to our homes?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Water All Around Us
activities.body: Water is a gift from nature. Surya and Barkha get water from taps at home and at school. These taps receive water through pipes. A tank can store water high on a terrace. A terrace is the high place where the tank is kept. From a well, water may be drawn with a pulley, hand pump or electric pump. A pulley is a way to lift water.
keyPoints: Water comes from taps at home and school.
Pipes carry water to these taps.
Water can also come from wells, tanks and tankers.
activities.explanation: You can now connect water sources, pipes, tanks, wells and tankers.

activities.prompt: A family has a well. Other homes get tanker water. How can both get water home?
steps: A pulley, hand pump, or electric pump can draw well water.
The well family can bring it home because well water may be brought home.
The tanker homes can receive water because a tanker delivers it.
So both families can receive water at home.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where do Surya and Barkha get water from taps?
options: At a well and a terrace
At home and at school
In a tanker and a tank
Only at the school
activities.explanation: Surya and Barkha get water from taps at home and at school.

activities.prompt: Match each place with what the lesson says about it.
pairs: A high place to store water
A pulley, hand pump or electric pump
activities.explanation: A tank was found on the roof. Tanks store water high on a terrace.

activities.prompt: All these taps get water through pipes.
activities.explanation: Yes. Pipes carry water to the taps at home and school.

activities.prompt: Surya and Barkha found a tank on the ______.
activities.hint: It is the place where the tank was found.
activities.explanation: Good spotting! The tank was found on the roof.

activities.prompt: Which one may draw water from a well?
options: A tanker
A tank
A pulley
A tap
activities.explanation: A pulley may draw water from a well. A hand pump or electric pump may do this too.

activities.prompt: Which statement is true about getting water?
options: It may be stored only in a tanker.
A pump may draw it from a well.
It must reach every home through pipes.
It is always difficult to get each day.
activities.explanation: A hand pump or electric pump may draw water from a well. Other homes may receive tankers.

activities.prompt: One family uses a well. Another uses a tanker. How can each get water?
options: The first draws from the well, and the second uses tanker delivery.
The second draws from the well, and the first uses tanker delivery.
The first uses school taps, and the second uses roof tanks.
The first uses a roof tank, and the second uses school taps.

why.The second draws from the well, and the: This swaps the two water-getting methods.
why.The first uses school taps, and the seco: School taps and roof tanks do not match this situation.
why.The first uses a roof tank, and the seco: School taps and roof tanks do not match this situation.

activities.explanation: Well water may be drawn and brought home.

activities.prompt: Some people have difficulty getting water every day. What can help some homes?
options: A tanker can deliver water to the home.
A tank can pull water from a well.
A pipe can draw water from a well.
A pulley can drive a tanker.

A tank stores water instead of pulling it from a well.
A pipe carries water to taps instead of drawing well water.
A pulley can draw well water but does not drive tankers.

activities.explanation: Some homes may get their water delivered in a tanker.

activities.prompt: Pipes carry water to Surya's home tap. A tanker brings water to another home. What can both do?
options: Both can bring water to homes.
Both can draw water from wells.
Both can carry water to school taps.
Both can store water on terraces.

Pipes carry water to taps, while well tools draw water.
Pipes carry tap water, but tankers deliver water to homes.
A roof tank stores water high on a terrace.

activities.explanation: Pipes carry tap water home, and tankers deliver water to homes.

lessons.sceneCaption: A well pulley provides access to water in Yercaud, Salem, India.

lessons.title: Water in Daily Lives and Storing Water

activities.prompt: How do we keep water ready at home when it doesn’t flow in?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Water Around Us
activities.body: Each household stores water for daily needs. We store it because it may not always be available. Some homes have no running water. People may bring water from a river or well, or get it from a tanker. Long ago, there were no pipes or taps anywhere. People made containers. We use vessels with different materials. Two buckets can hold water. A burst pipeline can leave a place without water.
keyPoints: Each household stores water for daily needs.
People can receive water from tankers.
Many vessels store water at home.
activities.explanation: Storing water helps us when water is not always available.

activities.prompt: A home has no running water. What should the family do after filling two buckets at a well?
steps: No running water means the home cannot count on a tap.
Two buckets can hold the water brought from the well.
The family carries them home because the water must be kept there.
Thus, the family stores water at home for daily use.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Keeping Water at Home
activities.body: Long ago, there were no pipes or taps anywhere in the world. People learned to make containers for storing water. Today, each household still stores water for daily use. We use many vessels at home. Water vessels are made from different materials. Two buckets can hold stored water for use. Storing water helps when it is not always available.
keyPoints: Long ago, no pipes or taps existed anywhere.
People learned to make water containers.
Many home vessels use different materials.
activities.explanation: Containers and vessels help us store water at home for daily use.

activities.title: Why Store Water?
activities.prompt: Why does each household store water?
options: To make new taps
For daily use
To stop the rain
To warm the river
activities.explanation: Each household stores water for daily use. Having it at home helps when water is not always available.

activities.title: Homes Without Running Water
activities.prompt: Some homes have no running water.
activities.explanation: Yes. Some places have no running water in homes.

activities.title: Bring Water Home
activities.prompt: In some places, people bring water from a ______ or well.
activities.hint: The answer names another place people bring water from.
activities.explanation: In some places, people must bring water from a river or well.

activities.title: Water at Home
activities.prompt: Match each clue to the matching detail.
pairs: Bring water from a river or well
Can leave a place without water
activities.explanation: Households store water for daily use, and some homes have no running water. People bring or receive water and keep it at home. A burst pipeline can leave a place without water.

activities.title: When a Pipeline Bursts
activities.prompt: A society pipeline bursts in a place. What may happen?
options: Water may stop reaching homes.
Homes may gain running water.
Pipes may store more water.
Vessels may repair pipes.
activities.explanation: A burst society pipeline can leave a place without water. Storing water at home helps in this situation.

activities.title: Pipes in the Past
activities.prompt: Long ago, every place had pipes and taps in homes.
activities.explanation: Long ago, there were no pipes or taps anywhere in the world. People learned to make containers for storing water.

activities.prompt: No running water reaches this home. Where can the family get water?
options: From a river or well.
From a tap inside the home.
From a tanker kept at home.
From a burst society pipeline.

This mistake assumes a home tap exists without running water.
This mistake mixes up a tanker and a water source.
A burst pipeline can leave the place without water.

activities.explanation: People there bring water from a river or well.

activities.prompt: A society pipeline bursts. What can happen to this place?
options: The place can have no water.
The place can have extra water.
The place can make new taps.
The place can fill every bucket.

This mistake thinks a broken pipe adds water.
This mistake thinks a burst pipe creates taps.
This mistake assumes buckets need a working pipeline.

activities.explanation: A burst pipeline can leave the place without water.

activities.prompt: This home has no running water. A family fills two buckets at a well. What next?
options: Keep the buckets at home for daily use.
Leave the buckets beside the well.
Empty them into a burst pipeline.
Wait for running water at home.

This mistake leaves the water where the family cannot use it.
This mistake puts water into a pipeline that cannot supply it.
This mistake ignores that the home has no running water.

activities.explanation: This is right because buckets hold stored water for use at home.

activities.prompt: Two home water vessels use different materials. Can both hold stored water?
options: Yes, both are water vessels.
Yes, only one is a vessel.
No, different materials cannot store water.
No, only buckets can hold water.

This mistake thinks only matching materials make a vessel.
why.No, different materials cannot store wat: This mistake wrongly links different materials with poor storage.
This mistake wrongly says buckets are the only water vessels.

activities.explanation: This is right because many vessels store water despite different materials.

lessons.title: Using Water and Saving Every Drop

activities.prompt: Can you discover how water helps us and how we can save every drop?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Water Is Precious
activities.body: Water reaches Earth as rain. We bring it to our homes and store it in many ways. We use water, and it helps us keep things clean. Water becomes dirty after we use it. So we cannot drink or cook with it. We can reuse waste water for watering plants or flushing toilets. We should reduce water use and reuse it whenever possible. Avoid adding too much soap or chemicals.
keyPoints: Rain brings water down to Earth.
Dirty water cannot be used for drinking or cooking.
Reuse waste water and reduce water use.
activities.explanation: Saving water helps us care for this precious gift.

activities.prompt: You have used water at home. What can you do with the dirty water instead of wasting it?
steps: After water is used, it becomes dirty.
Dirty water cannot be used for drinking or cooking, so keep it away from both.
Used water can instead water plants or flush toilets.
Reusing water whenever possible and reducing water use helps us save every drop.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: How does water come down to Earth?
options: As rain
From stored water
As waste water
As dirty water
activities.explanation: Well done! Rain is how water comes down to Earth.

activities.prompt: Water helps us keep things clean.
activities.explanation: Yes! Water helps us keep things clean.

activities.prompt: We can reuse waste water for ______ plants.
activities.hint: This word tells what waste water can do to plants.
activities.explanation: Waste water can be used for watering plants. This gives it another useful purpose.

activities.prompt: Match each part of the water story.
pairs: Water is brought in many ways
Water is kept in many ways
Can be watered with waste water
activities.explanation: You matched the water journey and its uses. Each pair comes from the lesson.

activities.prompt: Put the water story in order.
activities.explanation: This order follows arrival, bringing, storing, use, and reuse.

activities.prompt: Which pair shows uses of waste water?
options: Water plants; flush toilets
Make water dirty; add soap
Store water; bring rain
Cook food; clean things
activities.explanation: Waste water can water plants or flush toilets. These uses are given in the lesson.

activities.prompt: Adding too much soap or chemicals to water is a good idea.
activities.explanation: We should not add too much soap or other chemicals. Water is a precious gift.

activities.prompt: Which plan follows the lesson's advice?
options: Reduce use; reuse water; limit soap
Drink dirty water; add soap; waste water
Store rain; make it dirty; use once
Soap heavily; cook with dirt; stop reuse
activities.explanation: The lesson says to reduce use and reuse water whenever possible. It also says not to add too much soap or chemicals.

activities.prompt: Water has become dirty after use. What should you do?
options: Use it to water plants or flush toilets.
Use it for drinking or cooking.
Add soap, then use it for drinking.
Store it for drinking later.

Dirty water cannot be used for drinking or cooking.
This adds soap and uses dirty water for drinking.
Dirty water cannot be stored for drinking later.

activities.explanation: Used water can water plants or flush toilets.

activities.prompt: Dirty water has some soap in it. What should you do?
options: Use it for plants or toilets, without extra soap or chemicals.
Add extra soap, then use it for drinking.
Add more chemicals, then use it for cooking.
Store it, then use it for drinking later.

why.Add extra soap, then use it for drinking: This adds too much soap and uses dirty water for drinking.
why.Add more chemicals, then use it for cook: This adds chemicals and uses dirty water for cooking.
why.Store it, then use it for drinking later: Dirty water cannot be stored for drinking later.

activities.explanation: Waste water can water plants or flush toilets, without adding extra soap or chemicals.

lessons.title: Every Drop Counts

activities.prompt: How could a little water help our neighborhood?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Water Matters
activities.body: Water is sacred because it is essential for our survival. Sacred means deeply respected. Everyone should get clean drinking water anywhere and at any time. Some places have little rain and no big water bodies. People walk long distances to get water. We should not waste even a drop of water.
keyPoints: Water is essential for our survival.
Everyone should get clean drinking water anywhere and at any time.
We should not waste even a drop of water.
activities.explanation: Water is essential, so every drop matters.

activities.prompt: A class wants a birdbath for birds and insects without wasting water.
steps: Make a birdbath, because birds need water to drink and cool down.
Add stones and pebbles, because birds perch while insects use the water.
Change water often and scrub twice a week, because both steps matter.
Use every drop, because water is essential for our survival.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: A Helpful Birdbath
activities.body: A birdbath is a shallow plate with water for birds. Birds can drink and cool down there. A wide bucket less than 10 cm deep can hold the water. Stones help birds perch. Smaller pebbles help insects use the water. Change the water frequently and clean it with a scrubber twice a week.
keyPoints: Birds drink and cool down in a birdbath.
Stones help birds perch, while smaller pebbles help insects.
Change the water frequently and clean it twice a week.
activities.explanation: A birdbath helps birds and insects while keeping its water clean.

activities.title: Choose Wisely
activities.prompt: Which action follows the lesson?
options: Save every drop of water
Waste even clean drinking water
Make water less important
Stop sharing water with others
activities.explanation: We should not waste even a drop of water.

activities.title: Clean Water for Everyone
activities.prompt: Everyone should get clean drinking water anywhere and at any time.
activities.explanation: This is an important lesson for everyone.

activities.title: Water Outside
activities.prompt: Some homes keep water outside so that ______ people can have some.
activities.hint: People who need water.
activities.explanation: Some homes keep water outside for thirsty people.

activities.title: Match the Birdbath Parts
activities.prompt: Match each part of a birdbath to its job.
pairs: A wide bucket less than 10 cm deep
Use a scrubber twice a week
activities.explanation: Each part has a special job in the birdbath.

activities.title: Birdbath Steps
activities.prompt: Put these birdbath steps in order.
items: Put water in the shallow plate.
Let birds drink and cool down.
activities.explanation: First there is water, then birds use it. After that, change the water.

activities.title: Why Every Drop Counts
activities.prompt: Why does every drop of water count?
options: Because water is essential for our survival.
Because stones help birds to perch.
Because smaller pebbles help insects.
Because buckets can be 10 cm deep.
activities.explanation: Water is absolutely essential for our survival.

activities.prompt: A town has little rain and no big water bodies. What may happen?
options: People may walk long distances to get water.
People may find a new river after some rain.
People may see a big lake form nearby.
People may get water from nearby big lakes.

why.People may find a new river after some r: A little rain does not explain the long water journeys described.
The town has no big water bodies, so a lake should not appear.
why.People may get water from nearby big lak: The town has no big water bodies, so nearby lakes cannot supply water.

activities.explanation: In places with little water, people may walk long distances for it.

activities.prompt: A class wants to test how stones and pebbles help. Which plan is fairest?
options: Compare a birdbath with both to one without them.
Watch one birdbath with both and record visits.
Give one birdbath only stones and compare its visits.
Give one birdbath only pebbles and compare its visits.

why.Watch one birdbath with both and record: Watching one birdbath cannot show whether stones and pebbles help.
why.Give one birdbath only stones and compar: Testing only stones does not show the pebbles' part.
why.Give one birdbath only pebbles and compa: Testing only pebbles does not show the stones' part.

activities.explanation: Changing only stones and pebbles makes the comparison fair.

activities.prompt: A child scrubs a birdbath twice a week but never changes the water. What is wrong?
options: The water should also be changed frequently.
The birdbath should be scrubbed only once a week.
The smaller pebbles should be removed before cleaning.
The birdbath should hold much less water.

why.The birdbath should be scrubbed only onc: Twice a week is the stated cleaning frequency, not once a week.
why.The smaller pebbles should be removed be: Cleaning means scrubbing, not removing smaller pebbles.
why.The birdbath should hold much less water: The care facts do not say to hold less water.

activities.explanation: Changing water often and scrubbing twice a week are both needed.

activities.context: Riya watched the rain fall heavily on the ground near her home. She put a vessel outside to collect the rainwater and looked at it. The water looked dirty. Some of the rain soaked into the ground and some gathered in puddles. The rest flowed away under the soil and joined a small stream near the field. The stream would later join the river.
activities.prompt: Riya leaves her vessel outside for the whole heavy rain. What is most likely to happen?
options: The vessel keeps collecting rainwater, and the water may look dirtier.
The rainwater in the vessel will dry up by itself and disappear.
The vessel will fill with clean water because heavy rain washes everything away.
The rain will change direction and stop falling near the vessel.

why.The rainwater in the vessel will dry up: The rain water that falls near the vessel can carry dirt, so it may look dirtier.
why.The vessel will fill with clean water be: Rain water does not dry up on its own while it keeps falling.
why.The rain will change direction and stop: Rain may slant or change direction, but it still sends water down to the ground.

activities.explanation: Heavy rain sends a lot of water down, so the vessel keeps filling.

activities.context: Riya watched the rain fall heavily on the ground near her home. She put a vessel outside to collect the rainwater and looked at it. The water looked dirty. Some of the rain soaked into the ground and some gathered in puddles. The rest flowed away under the soil and joined a small stream near the field. The stream would later join the river.
activities.prompt: Why did some of the rainwater gather in puddles instead of soaking in?
options: That rainwater stayed on the surface of the ground.
That rainwater flowed under the soil to reach the stream.
That rainwater was stored under the ground between rocks and soil.
That rainwater came from the stream that joins the river.

why.That rainwater flowed under the soil to: Water that flows under the soil joins a stream or pond instead of forming puddles.
why.That rainwater was stored under the grou: Water stored under the ground between rocks and soil is below the surface, not in puddles.
why.That rainwater came from the stream that: The stream and river are places water flows to, not the source of puddle water.

activities.explanation: Water that does not soak in can gather in puddles on the ground.

activities.context: Riya watched the rain fall heavily on the ground near her home. She put a vessel outside to collect the rainwater and looked at it. The water looked dirty. Some of the rain soaked into the ground and some gathered in puddles. The rest flowed away under the soil and joined a small stream near the field. The stream would later join the river.
activities.prompt: Riya finds water stored under the ground between rocks and soil below where the rain fell. What is this water most likely to be?
options: Underground water that could flow into a well.
Water that is still falling from the clouds.
Water that has been collected in the vessel outside.
Water that is gathering in puddles on top of the ground.

why.Water that is still falling from the clo: Rain water has already fallen, so it is not still falling here.
why.Water that has been collected in the ves: Water in the vessel is above the ground and was collected there.
why.Water that is gathering in puddles on to: Puddle water sits on the surface, not under the ground.

activities.explanation: Water under the ground between rocks and soil is underground water.

activities.prompt: Explain why rainwater can be found in different places after the rain, such as in puddles, under the soil, and in streams.
activities.answer: Rain sends a lot of water down to the ground. Some of this rainwater gathers in puddles on the surface, some soaks into the ground, and some flows under the soil to join a stream or pond. Water can also be stored under the ground between rocks and soil.
points: Rain sends a lot of water down to the ground.
Some water gathers in puddles on the surface.
Some water soaks in and flows under the soil to a stream or pond.
Some water is stored under the ground between rocks and soil.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Surya and Barkha get water from taps at home and at school. Pipes carry water to all these taps. They find a tank on the roof and learn that a tank high on a terrace can store water. At a nearby well, water may be drawn with a pulley, hand pump or electric pump, and water from the well may be brought home. Some people have difficulty getting water every day, and some homes receive water delivered in a tanker.
activities.prompt: If the pipes to Surya and Barkha's home taps stop working, what would happen next?
options: The home taps would stop receiving water.
The roof tank would send water through the taps by itself.
The well would stop providing water to everyone.
The tanker would fill the tank even if no delivery was arranged.

why.The roof tank would send water through t: A tank stores water, but it is not said to send water through taps.
why.The well would stop providing water to e: Water from a well is drawn using a pulley or pump and is separate from the home taps.
why.The tanker would fill the tank even if n: A tanker delivery is an option for some homes, but it is not automatic.

activities.explanation: The pipes carry water to the taps, so they would no longer receive it.

activities.context: Surya and Barkha get water from taps at home and at school. Pipes carry water to all these taps. They find a tank on the roof and learn that a tank high on a terrace can store water. At a nearby well, water may be drawn with a pulley, hand pump or electric pump, and water from the well may be brought home. Some people have difficulty getting water every day, and some homes receive water delivered in a tanker.
activities.prompt: What best explains why the tank found on the roof can be used to store water?
options: It is high up on a terrace.
It is found at the same taps used at school.
It is used with a pulley to draw well water.
It is used to carry a tanker delivery home.

why.It is found at the same taps used at sch: The tank is on the roof, while school taps are places where water comes out.
why.It is used with a pulley to draw well wa: Pulleys and pumps draw water from a well, while a tank stores water.
why.It is used to carry a tanker delivery ho: A tanker delivers water; it is not something that the tank carries.

activities.explanation: Water can be stored in a tank that is high up on a terrace.

activities.context: Surya and Barkha get water from taps at home and at school. Pipes carry water to all these taps. They find a tank on the roof and learn that a tank high on a terrace can store water. At a nearby well, water may be drawn with a pulley, hand pump or electric pump, and water from the well may be brought home. Some people have difficulty getting water every day, and some homes receive water delivered in a tanker.
activities.prompt: If the pipes to a home's taps are not working, which option could still bring water to that home?
options: A tanker could deliver a supply of water to the home.
A pulley could pull water down from the roof tank to the home.
A hand pump could draw water from the home pipes into the home.
An electric pump could draw water from the school taps and send it home.

why.A pulley could pull water down from the: A pulley is used to draw water from a well, not from a roof tank.
why.A hand pump could draw water from the ho: A hand pump draws water from a well, while pipes carry water to taps.
why.An electric pump could draw water from t: An electric pump draws water from a well; it is not said to take water from school taps.

activities.explanation: Some homes may get their water delivered in a tanker.

activities.prompt: Explain how water reaches Surya and Barkha's taps at home and at school.
activities.answer: Water travels through pipes to the taps at Surya and Barkha's home. It also travels through pipes to the taps at school. The pipes are the route that brings water to all these tap places, whether the taps are at home or at school.
points: They get water from home taps.
They also get water from school taps.
Pipes carry water to the taps.
The pipes serve both home and school.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A family lives in a place where some homes have no running water. They keep water in vessels and two buckets for daily use. When water is not always available, they collect it from a river or well. Sometimes a water tanker delivers water that is stored at home. A burst society pipeline has left the area without water.
activities.prompt: The pipeline is still broken and the tanker is not delivering today. What should the family do to obtain more water?
options: Travel to the river or the well and fetch water.
Wait for water to flow through the broken pipeline.
Fill the household vessels from the burst pipeline.
Pour the stored water back into the river or well.

why.Wait for water to flow through the broke: A burst pipeline leaves the area without water.
why.Fill the household vessels from the burs: The burst pipeline is not a working water source.
why.Pour the stored water back into the rive: Pouring water back would waste the stored supply.

activities.explanation: People can bring water from a river or well.

activities.context: A family lives in a place where some homes have no running water. They keep water in vessels and two buckets for daily use. When water is not always available, they collect it from a river or well. Sometimes a water tanker delivers water that is stored at home. A burst society pipeline has left the area without water.
activities.prompt: The usual vessels at home are full after the tanker delivery. What can hold extra stored water for use?
options: The pair of buckets.
The burst society pipeline.
The water tanker.
The river or well.

A pipeline carries water and is described as burst.
A tanker delivers water rather than serving as a home container.
A river or well is a source, not a household storage container.

activities.explanation: Two buckets can hold stored water for use.

activities.prompt: Explain why families store water at home even when a tanker sometimes delivers it.
activities.answer: Water is not always available, and some homes have no running water. A tanker may bring water, but the family still needs to keep that water in vessels and two buckets for daily use. Stored water is especially helpful when a burst pipeline leaves the area without water.
points: Water is not always available.
Households keep water in vessels and two buckets.
Stored water is kept for daily use.
Stored water helps when a pipeline burst leaves an area without water.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A family receives rain that comes down to earth. They bring water from sources to their home and store it for uses. When they wash, water helps keep things clean, but it becomes dirty after use. They cannot use that dirty water for drinking or cooking. Instead, they reuse waste water for watering plants or flushing toilets. They also try to reduce their water use, and they do not add too much soap or other chemicals to water.
activities.prompt: What should the family do with the water that has become dirty after washing?
options: Water the plants or flush the toilet with it.
Use it for drinking or cooking.
Throw it away without using it again.
Mix in more soap and use it for drinking.

Dirty water cannot be used for drinking or cooking.
Throwing it away misses a chance to reuse it.
why.Mix in more soap and use it for drinking: Adding too much soap is wrong, and dirty water cannot be drunk.

activities.explanation: Reusing dirty water for plants or toilets is helpful.

activities.context: A family receives rain that comes down to earth. They bring water from sources to their home and store it for uses. When they wash, water helps keep things clean, but it becomes dirty after use. They cannot use that dirty water for drinking or cooking. Instead, they reuse waste water for watering plants or flushing toilets. They also try to reduce their water use, and they do not add too much soap or other chemicals to water.
activities.prompt: If the family wants to save every drop, which plan best follows the lesson?
options: Use smaller amounts, then find another use for the water.
Store all the water and never use any of it.
Use extra water so some is always left.
Add more soap and chemicals so the water lasts longer.

why.Store all the water and never use any of: Water should be used and reused, not only stored.
Using more water does not reduce water use.
why.Add more soap and chemicals so the water: We should not add too much soap or other chemicals.

activities.explanation: Reducing use and reusing water both help save every drop.

activities.prompt: How should the family reuse water after washing, and why should they not use it for drinking or cooking?
activities.answer: After washing, the family should reuse the dirty water for watering plants or flushing toilets. They should not drink or cook with it because water becomes dirty after use. They should also avoid adding too much soap or other chemicals, and they should try to use less water.
points: Dirty water can water plants.
Dirty water can flush toilets.
It cannot be used for drinking or cooking.
Use less water and avoid too much soap or chemicals.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: In a dry area, people walk long distances for water because there is little rain and no big water bodies. Homes keep water outside for thirsty people. The birdbath is a wide bucket less than 10 cm deep. Water lets birds drink and cool down. The family should change the water frequently and clean the bucket with a scrubber twice a week. They should not waste a drop.
activities.prompt: The family has not changed the birdbath water for a while. What should they do next?
options: Replace the water often and scrub the bucket two times each week.
Keep the old water and add more without cleaning it.
Empty the bucket and leave it dry.
Move the bucket somewhere that birds cannot reach it.

why.Keep the old water and add more without: Adding more water does not replace the old water or clean the container.
Birds need water in the birdbath to drink and cool down.
why.Move the bucket somewhere that birds can: Birds could not use the birdbath if it were moved out of their reach.

activities.explanation: This follows the advice to change the water frequently and clean the bucket twice a week.

activities.context: In a dry area, people walk long distances for water because there is little rain and no big water bodies. Homes keep water outside for thirsty people. The birdbath is a wide bucket less than 10 cm deep. Water lets birds drink and cool down. The family should change the water frequently and clean the bucket with a scrubber twice a week. They should not waste a drop.
activities.prompt: A thirsty visitor reaches a home in the dry area. What should the visitor do?
options: Use some of the water that the home has placed outside.
Use the birdbath water because it is closer.
Keep walking because the outside water is only for the family.
Wait for rain because clean drinking water is not needed now.

why.Use the birdbath water because it is clo: Birdbath water is for birds to drink and cool down.
why.Keep walking because the outside water i: The water outside is meant for thirsty people, not only for the family.
why.Wait for rain because clean drinking wat: Everyone should get clean drinking water and should not need to wait for rain.

activities.explanation: Homes keep water outside so that thirsty people can have some.

activities.prompt: Explain why people should not waste even a drop of water.
activities.answer: Water should not be wasted because it is absolutely essential for our survival. Everyone should get clean drinking water anywhere and at any time. Taking care not to waste even a drop helps people who need water, including those who must walk long distances to get it.
points: Water is essential for survival
Everyone should get clean drinking water anywhere and at any time
Not wasting water helps people who must walk long distances to get it
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Where can rainwater flow under the soil?
options: Into a household tap
Into a stream or pond
Onto a roof tank
Through a pulley
activities.explanation: Rainwater can flow under the soil and join a stream or pond.

activities.prompt: Rain may slant or change its direction.
activities.explanation: Rain does not always fall straight down.

activities.prompt: Rain may ______ or change its direction.
activities.hint: Choose the word from the lesson.
activities.explanation: The lesson says that rain may slant or change its direction.

activities.prompt: Put the rainwater journey in order.
items: Rain sends water down to the ground
The stream later joins a river
activities.explanation: Rainwater can soak into the ground and travel under the soil to water.

activities.prompt: Why do we store water?
options: Because it is always heavy
Because it is not always there
Because pipes are underground
Because taps give clean water
activities.explanation: We store water when it is not always available.

activities.prompt: We can use dirty water for drinking or cooking.
activities.explanation: Dirty water cannot be used for drinking or cooking.

activities.prompt: Match each birdbath item with its partner.
activities.explanation: Birdbaths help birds and insects, while stones help birds perch.

activities.prompt: What can we do with waste water?
options: Watering plants
Drinking it
Cooking food
activities.explanation: Waste water can be reused for watering plants or flushing toilets.

chapters.title: Food We Eat
chapters.summary: In this chapter: my favourite food and tastes; shirin learns about healthy food; foods for different seasons and places; why we drink water.

lessons.title: My favourite food and tastes

activities.prompt: What are your favourite foods, and what tastes do you love most?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Food, drinks and six tastes
activities.body: We enjoy different food and drink. Some are sweet or sour. Others are spicy or bitter. Chhappan bhog has 56 varieties. It is special festival food and prepared on special occasions. Its six tastes are sweet, spicy, astringent, sour, salty and bitter. Astringent is one taste. It honours guests, friends and family. We eat fruits, vegetables, rice, dal and roti. We drink milk, lassi and juice.
keyPoints: Food and drink can have different tastes.
Chhappan bhog has 56 varieties.
The six tastes make a good mixture.
activities.explanation: This lesson introduces favourite foods, drinks and the six tastes.

activities.prompt: A family is preparing for guests on an auspicious day. How can the meal suit guests with different tastes?
steps: The family wants to honour guests on an auspicious day.
Chhappan bhog is prepared for such occasions.
Its 56 varieties form a mixture of six tastes.
So each guest can find a favourite food to enjoy.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What is chhappan bhog?
activities.prompt: What is chhappan bhog according to the lesson?
options: Special festival food
Everyday drinking item
Fruit served with milk
Food for guests only
activities.explanation: Chhappan bhog is special food for festivals. It also honours guests, friends and family.

activities.title: Different choices
activities.prompt: People enjoy different kinds of food and drink.
activities.explanation: Yes. Different people enjoy different kinds of food and drink.

activities.title: How many varieties?
activities.prompt: A chhappan bhog has ______ varieties of food.
activities.hint: Find the number in the lesson.
activities.explanation: The lesson tells us that one chhappan bhog has 56 varieties of food.

activities.title: Food and drink matches
activities.prompt: Match each word or phrase with its correct detail.
pairs: people it is prepared to honour
activities.explanation: The pairs show foods, drinks and food prepared to honour guests.

activities.title: Foods in the lesson
activities.prompt: Put these foods in the order used in your book.
activities.explanation: Your book lists fruits first, then vegetables, rice, dal and roti.

activities.title: A tasty mixture
activities.prompt: What do the six tastes form in chhappan bhog?
options: A good mixture
A separate meal
A sweet drink
A single food
activities.explanation: The lesson says the six tastes form a good mixture.

activities.prompt: Chhappan bhog has six tastes. What can guests get at a festival?
options: A large mixture of many food varieties
A single sweet dish with no other foods
A plate of only fruits and vegetables
A drink menu with no food at all

why.A single sweet dish with no other foods: This wrongly treats the many varieties as one food.
why.A plate of only fruits and vegetables: This wrongly assumes the festival food contains only fruit and vegetables.
why.A drink menu with no food at all: This wrongly treats chhappan bhog as only a drink.

activities.explanation: This matches the 56 varieties and six tastes.

activities.prompt: One child likes sweet food. Another likes sour food. What should the host serve each child?
options: Offer both foods so each child can choose
Offer only sweet food because one asked
Offer only sour food because one asked
Offer one food and expect both to agree

why.Offer only sweet food because one asked: This wrongly ignores the child's wish for sour food.
why.Offer only sour food because one asked: This wrongly ignores the child's wish for sweet food.
why.Offer one food and expect both to agree: This wrongly assumes that both children want one food.

activities.explanation: This respects the two children's different tastes.

activities.prompt: Rice, dal, roti, fruit and vegetables are foods. Milk, lassi and juice are drinks. What should a family offer guests who enjoy different kinds?
options: Foods and drinks so everyone can choose
Only rice and roti because both are foods
Only milk and juice because both are drinks
One food and one drink for every guest

why.Only rice and roti because both are food: This wrongly ignores the drinks that people may enjoy.
why.Only milk and juice because both are dri: This wrongly ignores the foods that people may enjoy.
why.One food and one drink for every guest: This wrongly ignores the different choices people enjoy.

activities.explanation: Different guests can choose from both foods and drinks.

lessons.sceneCaption: Fifty-six dishes form a colourful and devotional festive food offering.

lessons.title: Shirin learns about healthy food

activities.prompt: What healthy foods helped Shirin grow strong and run faster?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Shirin meets a champion
activities.body: Shirin used to run very fast and faster than everyone in her class. She met a champion who had won many medals. The champion said she could become a champion if she practised a lot. She was also told to eat healthy food. Shirin practised, but often fell sick. After a few months, she could run faster than before.
keyPoints: The champion advised lots of practice.
Rice and potatoes were only part of her food.
Different foods supported a strong body.
After a few months, she ran faster.
activities.explanation: Practice and healthy food were both part of the champion's advice.

activities.prompt: Shirin practises a lot but often falls sick. What should she change about her food?
steps: Her practice should continue, because it can help her become a champion.
Rice and potatoes are good, but Shirin still needs other foods.
Vegetables, fruits, grains, dal, and nuts help build a strong, healthy body.
With healthy food, she could run faster after a few months.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Shirin's healthy food choices
activities.body: Shirin could eat foods made from grains such as rice, ragi, jowar, wheat and bajra. She was also told to eat pulses, or dal, and nuts. Different kinds of vegetables and fruits helped too. Food cooked at home was good for her. These foods helped build a strong and healthy body.
keyPoints: Eat foods made from grains.
Eat vegetables, fruits, dal and nuts.
Choose food cooked at home.
Eat many different kinds of foods.
activities.explanation: Shirin needed many different foods for a strong and healthy body.

activities.prompt: What did the champion tell Shirin to do?
options: Practise less and eat only fruit
Practise a lot and eat healthy food
Meet everyone and eat potatoes only
Practise little and eat only dal
activities.explanation: The champion advised Shirin to practise a lot. She also advised healthy food.

activities.prompt: Shirin was told to eat different kinds of vegetables and fruits.
activities.explanation: The champion told Shirin to eat different kinds of vegetables and fruits.

activities.prompt: ______ and potatoes were good foods for Shirin.
activities.hint: This food is made from a grain.
activities.explanation: The champion specifically said rice and potatoes were good foods for Shirin.

activities.prompt: Match each item with its description from the lesson.
activities.explanation: Ragi is a grain food, and dal is a pulse. Potatoes and home-cooked food were good for Shirin.

activities.prompt: Shirin only needed rice and potatoes to become strong and healthy.
activities.explanation: She needed many other foods as well. Different foods helped her have a strong and healthy body.

activities.prompt: Which list includes every food type Shirin was told to eat?
options: Rice, potatoes, vegetables, dal and nuts
Rice, vegetables, fruits, grains and nuts
Rice, vegetables, fruits, dal and grains
Rice, vegetables, fruits, dal and nuts
activities.explanation: She needed foods from grains, vegetables, fruits, pulses and nuts. The correct list includes each kind.

activities.prompt: Put Shirin's story in the correct time order.
items: Shirin used to run very fast
She practised a lot and often fell sick
After a few months, she ran faster
activities.explanation: She first ran very fast and later met the champion. She then practised a lot and often fell sick. After a few months, she ran faster.

activities.prompt: Shirin practises a lot but often falls sick. What food change should she make?
options: Eat varied healthy foods, including grains, dal, nuts, fruits, and vegetables.
Eat only rice and potatoes because the champion praised them.
Stop practising often because healthy food cannot help her run.
Eat only fruit and stop eating grains, dal, and nuts.

why.Eat only rice and potatoes because the c: She mistakes good foods for the only foods she needs.
why.Stop practising often because healthy fo: She wrongly thinks healthy food cannot help her running.
why.Eat only fruit and stop eating grains, d: She wrongly thinks fruit should replace grains, dal, and nuts.

activities.explanation: She needs many kinds of food to build a strong, healthy body.

activities.prompt: Children eat different foods and practise for different times. How can they make a fair food test?
options: Keep practice the same and change only their foods.
Keep food the same and change each child's practice time.
Change both food and practice for every child.
Stop all practice and compare only what they eat.

why.Keep food the same and change each child: This changes practice too, so the test cannot show food's effect.
why.Change both food and practice for every: Changing both food and practice hides which one caused a difference.
why.Stop all practice and compare only what: Stopping practice removes the practice part of the test.

activities.explanation: Keeping practice the same lets them compare the effect of food.

lessons.sceneAlt: A plate of roasted chicken, white rice, broccoli, orange cauliflower, potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, garlic and dried fruits.
lessons.sceneCaption: Roasted chicken with white rice and colorful vegetables provides many different foods to eat.

sceneCredit.text: Liat Portal for Foodie Disorder - Roasted chicken with vegetables and  by HaJunkiyada, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
sceneCredit.creator: HaJunkiyada

lessons.title: Foods for different seasons and places

activities.prompt: What foods and drinks do we enjoy in different seasons and places?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Foods change with seasons and places
activities.body: Foods change with the season and the place. In hot weather, we enjoy kulfi or ice-cream and tender coconut water. In winter, we eat warm foods, soups and stews, and enjoy hot drinks. Mangoes and melons come in summer, while apples come in winter. People across our country enjoy varied foods, and friends or family may find different foods when they travel.
keyPoints: Hot weather brings kulfi, ice-cream and tender coconut water.
Winter brings warm foods, soups, stews, hot drinks and apples.
Different places have different foods.
activities.explanation: This card shows how seasons and places change our food choices.

activities.prompt: A child sees different foods while travelling. How do seasons and places change foods?
steps: People in another part of the country may eat different foods.
Friends or family may find different foods when they travel.
Different fruits and vegetables are available in different seasons.
So, foods can change with both the season and the place.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which food do we love when it is hot?
options: kulfi
soup
stew
hot drink
activities.explanation: Excellent! Kulfi is a food we love in hot weather.

activities.prompt: We drink tender coconut water in summer.
activities.explanation: That is right. Tender coconut water is a summer drink.

activities.prompt: In winter, we eat warm foods, ______ and stew.
activities.hint: This food is warm and often comes as a bowl.
activities.explanation: Great! Soups and stews are warm winter foods.

activities.prompt: Match each season or place with its food.
activities.explanation: You matched foods with the right seasons and places.

activities.prompt: We get mangoes and melons in winter.
activities.explanation: Good try! Mangoes and melons come in summer.

activities.prompt: People staying in another part of our country may eat foods ______ from ours.
activities.hint: People in different places enjoy different foods.
activities.explanation: Exactly! People in another part may eat foods different from ours.

activities.prompt: What may friends or family find when they travel to other places?
options: different foods
mangoes only
apples only
hot drinks only
activities.explanation: Well done! Travellers may find foods different from those at home.

activities.prompt: Claim: all places eat the same food. Which observation shows a flaw?
options: Friends find only the same foods when they travel.
Friends find no foods when they travel.
Friends find different foods when they travel.
Friends find different foods only at home.

why.Friends find only the same foods when th: This mistake says travel does not bring different foods.
This mistake thinks travel removes all food choices.
why.Friends find different foods only at hom: This mistake limits different foods to the home place.

activities.explanation: This is right because friends may find different foods when travelling.
