lessons.title: Keeping Our Surroundings Clean

activities.prompt: What simple pledge can help our home, school, and neighbourhood stay clean?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Our cleanliness pledge
activities.body: We can pledge to keep ourselves and our surroundings clean. National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 January. We should not create too much waste. We should manage our waste and dispose of it properly. This can build a cleaner and greener world. Our aim is, “Want not, Waste not.” Here, dispose of it properly means putting waste away in the right way.
keyPoints: Keep ourselves and our surroundings clean.
Remember, “Want not, Waste not.”
Manage waste and dispose of it properly.
activities.explanation: Proper waste disposal can build a cleaner and greener world.

activities.prompt: Your class has rubbish after a party. What should everyone do?
steps: The class should pledge to stay clean because each person can help.
Make less waste because our aim is, “Want not, Waste not.”
Dispose of the waste properly because this helps keep places clean.
Therefore, the class can help build a cleaner and greener world.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What helps you keep your room clean?
options: Keeping it tidy
Leaving it untidy
Making more waste
Keeping waste at home
activities.explanation: Keeping our room tidy helps us keep it clean.

activities.prompt: National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 ______.
activities.hint: Write the name of the month.
activities.explanation: National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 January.

activities.prompt: Match each place with the clean-up duty it has.
activities.explanation: We can help keep our home, neighbourhood, school, city and country clean.

activities.prompt: Put these waste-handling steps in order.
items: Remember not to create too much waste
activities.explanation: First, create less waste. Then manage it and dispose of it properly.

activities.prompt: A student manages waste and disposes of it properly. What can this help build?
options: A cleaner and greener world
A cleaner and dirtier world
A greener and noisier world
A dirtier and warmer world
activities.explanation: Proper waste disposal can build a cleaner and greener world.

activities.prompt: Which action best follows “Want not, Waste not.”?
options: Create less waste
Keep every room very tidy
Clean all neighbourhood roads
Help keep our country clean
activities.explanation: Remembering not to create too much waste follows our aim.

activities.prompt: National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 January. A child says it comes after January ends. What is the best reply?
options: No, 30 January is still part of January.
No, January has no day for cleanliness.
Yes, January ends before 30 January.
Yes, the clean day must come in another month.

This mistake thinks the clean day lies outside its own month.
This mistake gets the order of the month and day wrong.
why.Yes, the clean day must come in another: This mistake thinks a named day cannot be inside its named month.

activities.explanation: This is right because 30 January comes before January ends.

activities.prompt: We can pledge to keep ourselves and our surroundings clean. Which action best keeps this pledge?
options: Make a pledge, because saying it is the only action needed.
Keep only the room clean, because other places do not matter.
Throw waste anywhere, because it cannot spoil the area.
Dispose of waste properly and keep the surroundings clean.

why.Make a pledge, because saying it is the: This mistake thinks a pledge works without any action.
why.Keep only the room clean, because other: This mistake thinks clean surroundings include only our room.
why.Throw waste anywhere, because it cannot: This mistake thinks waste left carelessly will not spoil places.

activities.explanation: This is right because proper disposal helps keep our surroundings clean.

activities.prompt: Our aim should be, “Want not, Waste not.” What should we do with things we do not need?
options: Use what we have instead of creating more waste.
Get more anyway, because having extra things is helpful.
Throw away what we have, because new things are better.
Make extra waste, because waste does not matter.

why.Get more anyway, because having extra th: This mistake thinks extra things help us waste less.
why.Throw away what we have, because new thi: This mistake forgets that throwing things away creates waste.
why.Make extra waste, because waste does not: This mistake thinks waste has no effect on our surroundings.

activities.explanation: This is right because we should not create too much waste.

activities.prompt: We should manage our waste and dispose of it properly. What is likely to happen in a neighbourhood?
options: It can become cleaner and greener because waste is disposed properly.
It will stay dirty because proper disposal cannot help.
It will get cleaner because proper disposal makes waste disappear.
It will get dirtier because proper disposal adds more waste.

why.It will stay dirty because proper dispos: This mistake thinks proper disposal has no effect on places.
why.It will get cleaner because proper dispo: This mistake thinks proper disposal makes all waste disappear.
why.It will get dirtier because proper dispo: This mistake thinks disposal adds rubbish instead of managing it.

activities.explanation: This is right because proper disposal can build a cleaner, greener world.

activities.prompt: Each of us can help keep our home and neighbourhood clean. A child says only grown-ups can help. What is the best reply?
options: The child cannot help because cleaning is grown-up work.
Only the home matters because neighbourhoods do not count.
The child should wait because adults must do all work.
The child can help too because each person can help.

why.The child cannot help because cleaning i: This mistake thinks children cannot help keep places clean.
why.Only the home matters because neighbourh: This mistake thinks only our home matters, not our neighbourhood.
why.The child should wait because adults mus: This mistake thinks cleaning belongs only to adults.

activities.explanation: This is right because each of us can help our home and neighbourhood.

activities.prompt: We can also help keep our school, city and country clean. Keeping our room tidy helps us keep it clean. What does tidying show?
options: A student can help many places, starting with a tidy room.
A tidy room helps, but schools and cities do not matter.
Only rooms can help, so schools and countries cannot.
A dirty room is needed to help clean other places.

why.A tidy room helps, but schools and citie: This mistake thinks our help stops at our room.
why.Only rooms can help, so schools and coun: This mistake thinks rooms cannot help keep other places clean.
why.A dirty room is needed to help clean oth: This mistake thinks a room must be dirty to help us.

activities.explanation: This is right because tidy rooms help, and our help can reach many places.

activities.prompt: Explain why garbage around homes can be a problem and what people should do about it.
activities.answer: Garbage piles can form when thrown-away waste is not managed. They are seen around homes, schools and neighbourhoods, and garbage around people can make them ill. This is why we need to learn how to manage waste. People can learn from other people and places that manage waste well.
points: Some thrown-away waste ends up in garbage piles.
Garbage piles are seen around homes, schools and neighbourhoods.
Garbage around people can make them ill.
We can learn from people and places that manage waste well.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A child often buys snacks in wrappers and drinks in plastic bottles. The family uses plastic bags when shopping, even though cloth bags can help reduce waste. The child’s room also has old toys and books that other people could need. At a Cleanliness Drive, people share useful things with others. The family wants to follow the first rule of reducing waste, but the child wants to buy many new things.
activities.prompt: What should the family do with the old toys and books?
options: Give them to people who could use them instead of discarding them.
Keep them unused even though other people could need them.
Throw them away because they are no longer wanted.
Buy new ones so the old ones can be replaced.

why.Keep them unused even though other peopl: Keeping them does not help anyone who needs them.

activities.explanation: Sharing helps others use the items.

activities.context: A child often buys snacks in wrappers and drinks in plastic bottles. The family uses plastic bags when shopping, even though cloth bags can help reduce waste. The child’s room also has old toys and books that other people could need. At a Cleanliness Drive, people share useful things with others. The family wants to follow the first rule of reducing waste, but the child wants to buy many new things.
activities.prompt: Why would the child create more waste by buying many new things?
options: The extra purchases would create more items that eventually need to be thrown away.
The extra purchases would make every wrapper disappear.
The extra purchases would turn plastic bottles into cloth bags.
The extra purchases would fill the Cleanliness Drive with useful things.

why.The extra purchases would make every wra: Purchases do not make wrappers disappear.
why.The extra purchases would turn plastic b: Buying things does not change bottles into bags.
why.The extra purchases would fill the Clean: New purchases do not necessarily become useful items at the Drive.

activities.explanation: Buying more things leads to throwing away more things.

activities.prompt: Explain why buying only what we need helps to reduce waste.
activities.answer: Buying only what we need helps us create less waste. If we buy more things than we really need, we are likely to throw away more things later. The first rule is to reduce the amount of waste we create, so choosing carefully and buying only necessary things supports this rule.
points: Explains that unnecessary buying creates more waste.
Links buying more to throwing away more.
States that buying only what is needed reduces waste.
Identifies reducing waste as the first rule.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: How does reusing old clothes and giving them to others help, and why can old newspapers and cloth be used for gift wrapping?
activities.answer: Reusing old clothes keeps them useful. They can be made into a quilt and bags, and some can be given to people who need them. Old newspapers and cloth can wrap gifts, which reduces waste and gives the gift a personal touch.
points: Old clothes can be made into a quilt and bags.
Clothes can be given to people who need them.
Newspaper and cloth can be reused for gift wrapping.
Reused wrapping reduces waste and adds a personal touch.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A visitor compares places known for cleanliness. In Silluk, a village in Arunachal Pradesh, the roads are clean, with no trash on the roadsides, in corners, or in open spaces. The tree-lined streets feel like a garden. Silluk has received an award for managing its waste well and is called a zero waste village. Chhota Narena was among the first villages to become waste-free, while Indore and Mysuru stand out as clean cities.
activities.prompt: If waste management in Silluk became careless, what would the village be most likely to experience?
options: Rubbish could collect in places around the roads again.
The award would keep the roads clean without any further work.
The tree-lined streets would begin to feel less like a garden.
Silluk would remain a zero-waste village without any change.

why.The award would keep the roads clean wit: An award cannot guarantee clean roads if waste is not managed properly.
why.The tree-lined streets would begin to fe: Careless waste management could spoil the clean, garden-like feeling of the streets.
why.Silluk would remain a zero-waste village: A zero-waste village would be at risk if waste management stopped working well.

activities.explanation: Good waste management helps stop rubbish from gathering around the village.

activities.context: A visitor compares places known for cleanliness. In Silluk, a village in Arunachal Pradesh, the roads are clean, with no trash on the roadsides, in corners, or in open spaces. The tree-lined streets feel like a garden. Silluk has received an award for managing its waste well and is called a zero waste village. Chhota Narena was among the first villages to become waste-free, while Indore and Mysuru stand out as clean cities.
activities.prompt: If Chhota Narena wanted to follow Silluk's example, what would be the most important step?
options: Rely on receiving an award rather than handling waste carefully.
Handle its waste carefully so that the village can become waste-free.
Make tree-lined streets the only goal for the village.
Use the name of a clean city instead of managing the village's waste.

why.Rely on receiving an award rather than h: Careful waste handling would help Chhota Narena become waste-free.
why.Make tree-lined streets the only goal fo: Tree-lined streets are a feature, but they do not remove the need for waste control.
why.Use the name of a clean city instead of: A clean-city name cannot manage waste or make a village waste-free.

activities.explanation: An award recognizes good management but cannot replace it.

activities.prompt: Explain why Silluk can be called a zero waste village.
activities.answer: Silluk is called a zero waste village because it manages waste well. Its roads are clean, with no trash on the roadsides, in corners, or in open spaces. It has also received an award for managing its waste well.
points: Explains that Silluk manages waste well.
Uses the clean roads and absence of rubbish as evidence.
Mentions the award for good waste management.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: In a village, separate bins stood near the market. One bin was green and the other was blue. Fruit peels, eggshells and a dry branch went into the green bin. A discarded glass jar was placed in the blue bin. Green-bin waste can become compost, while discarded glass can be used to make new objects.
activities.prompt: If the dry branch had been put in the blue dustbin instead, what would happen next?
options: It would not rot and mix with soil to become compost.
It would rot and mix with soil just like food scraps.
It would provide food for plants and tiny soil animals.
It would be used to make a new object through recycling.

why.It would rot and mix with soil just like: Rotting into soil belongs to green-bin waste.
why.It would provide food for plants and tin: Compost, not blue-bin waste, feeds plants and animals.
why.It would be used to make a new object th: Recycling uses discarded metal, glass, plastic and paper.

activities.explanation: Only green-bin waste follows the compost process.

activities.context: In a village, separate bins stood near the market. One bin was green and the other was blue. Fruit peels, eggshells and a dry branch went into the green bin. A discarded glass jar was placed in the blue bin. Green-bin waste can become compost, while discarded glass can be used to make new objects.
activities.prompt: If villagers put fruit peels in the blue dustbin instead of the green dustbin, what would happen to the peels?
options: They would miss the compost process and would not provide food through compost.
They would be used to make new objects through recycling.
They would rot and mix with soil inside the blue dustbin.
They would provide food for tiny soil animals even without compost.

why.They would be used to make new objects t: Recycling does not include fruit peels.
why.They would rot and mix with soil inside: Only green-bin waste rots and mixes with soil.
why.They would provide food for tiny soil an: Compost provides food for plants and tiny soil animals.

activities.explanation: Fruit peels become compost when placed in green bins.

activities.prompt: Explain why green-bin waste can help plants and tiny soil animals.
activities.answer: Green-bin waste rots easily and mixes with soil. When it is added to soil, it becomes compost. This compost provides food for plants and tiny soil animals.
points: Green-bin waste rots easily.
It mixes with soil.
It becomes compost.
Compost provides food for plants and tiny soil animals.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: On National Cleanliness Day, a child saw a lot of waste in the neighbourhood and in the child’s room. The child promised to keep both places clean and followed the idea, “Want not, Waste not.” The child did not make extra rubbish, looked after the waste already made, and put it away correctly. By keeping the room in order, the child showed how every person can improve the home, neighbourhood, school, city and country.
activities.prompt: What is likely to happen if the child continues managing the waste properly?
options: A cleaner and greener world will be built.
The neighbourhood will become dirtier and wasteier.
Keeping the room clean will become more difficult.
The home and neighbourhood will remain unchanged.

why.The neighbourhood will become dirtier an: Leaving waste unmanaged would make the surroundings dirtier.
why.Keeping the room clean will become more: Keeping the room tidy helps the child keep it clean.
why.The home and neighbourhood will remain u: Proper waste management helps improve our surroundings.

activities.explanation: Proper waste disposal can build a cleaner and greener world.

activities.context: On National Cleanliness Day, a child saw a lot of waste in the neighbourhood and in the child’s room. The child promised to keep both places clean and followed the idea, “Want not, Waste not.” The child did not make extra rubbish, looked after the waste already made, and put it away correctly. By keeping the room in order, the child showed how every person can improve the home, neighbourhood, school, city and country.
activities.prompt: Why should the child keep the room tidy?
options: It helps the child keep the room clean.
It means the room no longer needs cleaning.
It makes extra waste easier to create.
It means waste no longer needs proper disposal.

why.It means the room no longer needs cleani: A tidy room still needs to be kept clean.
Tidying does not mean creating more waste.
why.It means waste no longer needs proper di: Waste still needs to be managed and disposed of properly.

activities.explanation: Keeping a room tidy helps us keep it clean.

activities.prompt: How does managing waste properly help the world?
activities.answer: Managing waste and disposing of it properly helps build a cleaner and greener world. We should remember not to create too much waste, because our aim should be, “Want not, Waste not.” Each of us can help keep our home and neighbourhood clean.
points: Waste is managed and disposed of properly.
A cleaner and greener world is built.
We avoid creating too much waste.
Each person can help keep surroundings clean.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Taking Charge of Waste

activities.title: Burning Plastic
activities.prompt: What can happen when plastic burns?
options: It becomes compost.
It releases harmful gases.
It makes clean roads.
It fills water with germs.
activities.explanation: Burning plastic releases harmful gases.

activities.title: Garbage and Health
activities.prompt: Garbage around people can make them ill.
activities.explanation: Garbage around people can make them ill.

activities.title: National Cleanliness Day
activities.prompt: National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 ______.
activities.hint: This is the first month of the year.
activities.explanation: National Cleanliness Day is held on 30 January.

activities.title: Dustbin Partners
activities.prompt: Match each waste word with its partner.
activities.explanation: Green-bin waste becomes compost. Metal, glass and plastic can be recycled into new objects.

activities.title: Waste-care Steps
activities.prompt: Put these waste-care steps in order.
items: Make new objects from discarded materials
activities.explanation: Reducing waste is the first rule. Separate materials, then make new objects through recycling.

activities.title: Silluk's Waste Success
activities.prompt: Which statement about Silluk is true?
options: Silluk is known as a clean city.
Silluk has trash in its open spaces.
Silluk is a zero waste village.
Silluk received an award for poor waste management.
activities.explanation: Silluk is called a zero waste village. It received an award for managing waste well.

activities.title: Buying Wisely
activities.prompt: Buying more things always reduces the waste we create.
activities.explanation: Buying more things makes us throw away more things.

activities.title: Old Sarees, New Quilts
activities.prompt: Our grandparents made ______ from old sarees.
activities.hint: A warm covering made from pieces of cloth.
activities.explanation: Our grandparents made quilts from old sarees and bags from old clothes.

activities.title: Give Old Things a New Use
activities.prompt: Match each old item with a clever new use.
activities.explanation: Old sarees, clothes, newspapers and calendars can all be reused.

activities.title: Want Not, Waste Not
activities.prompt: What should you do before buying something?
options: Buy more things than before.
Buy only wrapped food and drinks.
Throw away useful old things.
Buy only what you need.
activities.explanation: Buying more things makes us throw away more things. We should buy only what we need.
